Since only 28 buildings can be erected on one planet, you must choose carefully what to build as your colony grows, or tear down old buildings to make place for others.

With only one planet to begin with, your typical course of action is to build a spaceport and construct a colony ship, loaded with up to four of your existing colonists. As they arrive on a new planet, you can choose to establish a colony if the environment looks good; some planets have lots of grass land for population growth, others have mineral resources while some consist of mostly desert or ice. There are special structures to melt ice or irrigate desert, but building these cost resources.

A large number of space ships may be built, from small fighters to large destroyers and battlestars. The warships will fight other spaceships or destroy ground defences, while colony ships and troop transports carry humans. The latter is necessary to conquer a planet owned by the enemy. You can also construct spy satellites to send to other systems, where they will indicate if there are buildings on the ground or if there are ships in orbit, so that you don't have to send a group of unarmed colonists into the arms of the machines. Installing stargates in the orbit of a star allows instantaneous travel between systems, at the cost of energy.

If the machines invade a human planet, they destroy unnecessary structures and put the humans at work to supply the resources needed to construct machine soldiers and their ships. Their mothership moves around from system to system and is immensely stronger than any human ship.

211996.overview: Cricket sport managerial game written in HiSoft BASIC. Game design & coding by Paul Dowers. The game concentrates on the strategy and offers up plenty of relevant statistics. The game has been designed and developed by a true fan of the sport. It replicates everything that a real manager has to deal with.

212057.overview: A split screen two player game in which you must seek out and kill your opponent. Also has modem support.

212059.overview: Adaptation of well known table game that you play with a paper and pencil. Includes replay.

212060.overview:
Climbing Up is a shareware strategy/board game based on a popular board game of the same name.

It was developed by Huckstepp Software and published by Alternative Realities in 1996.

The game was the sequel to the game Falling Down, which was released the year prior to this.

212062.overview: Conquest is an Amiga strategy game released in 1995 by Amiga Action set in the year 66 B.C., where Julius Caesar has risen to rule the Roman Empire preparing for...CONQUEST.

212063.overview: Conquest Remix is an Amiga strategy game released in 1997, an updated version of the previously released Conquest game. This is the remix.

212064.overview:
CRAZY PRIEST, initially previewed as a playable demo at the RetroKomp/Load Error 2015 demo party, was released as a full PD/freeware game two years later at the RetroKomp/Load Error 2017 demo party in Poland. The game was ranked a very respectable 3rd in the RetroKomp GameDev Compo.
 Consist of 2 modes - single player and multiplayer. Seeking...collect and destroy!

212065.overview: C.Y.A.D is an abbreviation for 'Controlled Yellow Automated Device'. A super-hard puzzle game with simple graphics.

212066.overview: Significantly harder than its predecessor, C.Y.A.D. II features 49 new levels. Your goal is unchanged from the first game: Collect all diamonds and then get to the exit. C.Y.A.D. II introduces new gameplay elements like switches, blocks you can push, laser cannons that must be destroyed, and color-coded locks for which you need to retrieve keys.

212104.overview: Świąteczna awaria is an arcade platform game for up to three players. Mischievous penguin has stolen Santa's sleigh with gifts moments before Christmas. To save Christmas the player must collect the designated number of yellow packages, avoiding penguins, birds, wastebaskets, computers and other hostile creatures. In addition to jumping ability each of the three main characters (Santa, snowman, bear) has a unique temporarily stunning weapon (star, snow ball, colorful ball) and may use numerous power ups (long jumping, extra weapon, shield, fast running, temporary paralysis of all opponents). Occasionally defeated enemy pops up a green package. Gathering it moves to one of two timed mini-games: find two same pictures and find one designated picture. Passing a mini-game is rewarded with an extra life. Originally released as a coverdisk\covermount for Amiga Computer Studio 2/98 in Poland. It was eventually released worldwide in 2008.

212129.overview: A 2D Platformer created using AMOS and TOME by Richard Moore, it was inspired by Charlie Chimp. An updated version was released in 1998.

212152.overview: Head to head dueling game, find a buddy or a rival and pummel them info submission.

212154.overview: A top-down view racing game from Brian G. Vodnik and Henry F. Grosch of Realism Entertainment, which was released commercially in 1990, but was incorrectly included in the Nordlicht PD catalogue: spiele 7-01.

212159.overview: Can you handle Tetris in all the dimensions? You've got to build complete planes out of the pieces falling in the playing space. If a certain number of planes are filled, you get to go to the next round. If the play space fills to the top, the game ends. Initially designed by Fred Bayer with graphics by Oliver Siebert for full commercial release, previously interested suitors fell away when a similar game was released, so this game was released as Shareware in 1992.

212162.overview: Head out to your private fishing spot, pick the best lure and line type for the water and reel them in.

212262.overview: Or how Bonus McPhoneface got himself on another world, a short Another World clone that combines shooting, platforming, and puzzle-solving elements.

212263.overview:
Message from StarCom:

Galactic Outpost G-109 reported a large alien vessel entering the outer rim of the galaxy. Gortly after transmission G-109 was destroyed. Two Federation Battle Ships were sent to investigate but were also destroyed. The alien vessel appears immune to all current weapon systems. Reports show that at current trajectory and velocity it will reach Earth in three days. You are our last hope Captain! We will transport you over!

212268.overview: A multi-scrolling space shooter where the enemies are all around you and the mission is to kill 'em all. You can overhead your guns if you fire too much. Enemies have homing missiles as well as lots of other ordinance to use against you and they attack in a coordinated fashion to take you off guard and overwhelm you with close range missiles. .

212298.overview:
A combined Tron-Artillery game. You make track of worms, but with weapons. All 30 players have 5 weapons of their own and automatic shields and 3 speeds during the game. You can make Lava Storms, Airstrikes and trillions of other weapons. Cephalo Tron is built based on the game Stratoplex: 3D Tron.
This is how the creator Pete W. Stronsky himself presents the game. Many of you were probably surprised by the description of the "Tron-Artillery game". I'll explain right away, this is a game in which you have your own ray that is still advancing and growing. Your goal is to keep the beam from hitting the walls of the arena or your opponent; when that happens, you're done. You probably think, it's impossible, I can't stand dodging for more than a minute. Don't worry, Pete W. Stronsky solved it brilliantly, because you can use weapons. And it then proceeds with the beam where it is cleared of others. So to those weapons. So each player has five different ones.

212299.overview: You were hired by Getaway 3000 to help Indirect Software to realize their outstanding Power Amigo computer, with a 4D chip, one million megabytes of FAM a 68090 at 9 million Mhz. With it comes the games Rickman 4D, Tomb Rider and Capital Love. If you fail this mission you're fired, other wiser you're still fired but you're rich!! You start in the village of Lilypad. You've got to break into the PC headquarters to somehow snatch the PCs plans for the future from Billy Gates. This way Indirect Software may do the necessary changes to launch the great Power Amigo 2, so it can be better than the Penteum 233 BMX. Go forth and adventure!

212300.overview: A sliding tile puzzle game based on the game of the same name for the C64. This version is only 20 levels, the object on each level is to get the bomb to the drip to extinguish it. The bomb will start on one side of the screen with the drip at the bottom. You must shuffle the tiles to create a pathway to the drop. Each level has 2 time limits which are displayed as sliding bars at the bottom of the Info Panel. The top one is the time remaining before the bomb is launched and begins its movement along the pathways. You can launch the bomb earlier by clikcing R-Mouse, Fire or space. The remaining time before will be awarded to you as a bonus should you complete the level. The bottom time limit is before the bomb explodes, you can also look at the fuse for an indicator of remaining time.

212301.overview: CyberMan is a Dutch puzzle style game like the old Boulder Dash: you need to reach the exit, located in the upper corner right of the screen, clearing the way safely there by pushing the correct blocks.

212388.overview: A basic, German language horizontally scrolling space shooter set in the year 2294. You have at least kill 40% of the enemies or destroy the meteors on the levels to finish the level.

212399.overview: A first person RPG for the Amiga, originally the final entry in the Black Dawn series though it would eventually be followed by Black Dawn Rebirth in 2019.

212428.overview: An overhead racing game that went through many versions and was released under several names for both NTSC and PAL. .

212429.overview: So many have tried to make a "game like Scorched Earth, only better" and few actually achieve that goal. This is one game that meets and exceeds the promise. Created by Mike Boeh and released in 1994.

212430.overview: An AMOS game for up to 4 players by Chris Good and published by Valour Tech. An overhead shooter, the bad guy is on screen somewhere, but you can't always see them if they are camouflaged. Take them out and win in a gun fight in close quarters.

212431.overview: A Columns clone where you try to rotate the incoming colors to match 3 on the colors already on the field of play, with 4 difficulty setting and up to 4 players in game. Ken Ward is to blame for the name of it. Included in Assassins 55 compilation.

212432.overview:
A one or two player puzzle game published by Silmarils in 1992, developed by Mac Soft. In this puzzle game you have to match a predefined colored pattern so that you fill a certain percentage with the rotatable fragments you have before you run out of matching fragments.

For example, in level 1 you have a 12x12 square, whereby the outer ring is purple, then blue, then red, then green, and finally a yellow block in the center.

Now you have a fragment for placing into the square, which you can rotate in any of the four directions. Once you placed it, those colored blocks will become gray and can't be used anymore. This also means that the next fragment must be placed totally into the colored area, overlapping isn't possible. And of course, you can only place them in a matching area of colored blocks.

And here comes the problem. Those fragments aren't just a square, they can be in unusual complex forms, and you have to carefully think where to place them, because once set, they can't be removed. And on top of this, you only have a few seconds to think. If the timer for a fragment runs to zero, you get a new fragment, but only if you have a bomb remaining, which is used when the time runs out. When you start a level, you have 5 bombs available.

Good news are that you normally don't have to fill all blocks, before you start the level, the game will tell you how much, in percent, you have to fill.

The game offers 100 different levels, one more complex then the other. This means, that the basic geometric figure will be more complex, but also the colored patterns inside the figure.

After completing a level, you get a level code for the following level, so you don't have to play all 100 levels in one row.

212433.overview: The rules of Colorix is to arrange a given order of coloured balls in a limit of time. It’s one more release like the rules by the Thailon game Atomix. A level editor is included.

212434.overview: Cosmic Battles is a tactical combat simulator based on the Star Trek game Cosmic Balance. In the game, you design ships and send them into combat. First you design, then you battle test. 6 included scenarios.

212435.overview: The game is two-player only where players must find each other in a maze and shoot each other to bits. The game is reviewed in the PD section of CU Amiga, April 1996. The game was written by Asa Margetts and has a built in level creator.

212436.overview: A German-Language two-player action game from Roland Weber & Kim Troldner. At the center of crush is the duel between two players. both use a joystick to steer their figure across a playing field. On this there are stones that can be pushed by a playing figure standing next to it in the direction of view. The aim of the game is to crush your opponent with a stone.

212443.overview: This feels like an updated version of the 1987 Pac-Man clone from 1987, this one was released in 1992 by Dave Baldwin and appears on the original Assassins disk. It has your normal dot gobbler, avoiding a similar quartet of ghosts.  In this one the ghosts do not hesitate to follow through the tunnel and speed is somewhat variable. The sound effects are the only letdown in this, as they are strange and unrelated sound samples.

212477.overview: A difficult challenge, aliens are popping up al over the maze. you can see where by the white transport dots. Keep your level of ammunition up by grabbing the red gun symbols, which pop up when you are getting low on ammo. So make every shot count!

212478.overview:
Colours is a fast-paced puzzle game in which the player eliminates coloured squares that are approaching the centre area from 4 sides.

In order to eliminate the other colours, you must point your piece at it and 'fire'. If the colour is the same colour as your piece, the square is eliminated, as well as all of the shapes of the same colour behind it, until your piece hits a piece of a different colour. If the square is of a different colour, or it is hit when collecting a line of similar shapes, your piece exchanges colours with the shape.

Features include a high score table and a serial-link option for two players.

212480.overview: A very simple Breakout style game with a few extras from Peter Bakota, released to PD in 1993.

212701.overview: A poker fruit/slot machine style game created by Saen Software in 1992.

212702.overview: A Dutch language, single person fruit/slot machine game created by E. Kramer, Joep Grooten  and  Guus Hildesheim, who did the graphics for this game, was sysop of the 'BBS de Saen', a Dutch modem-based bulletin board system (BBS), which published this game.

212703.overview:
Licenseware gambling games collection includes: 

- FruitMachine
- Poker
- Craps
- Blackjack
- Roulette

212704.overview: Choose your coalition pilot and head out to battle, well the battle will be coming straight at you. Defend the position against the enemy at all costs!

212706.overview:
Coque And Kieagua Rally is a game I have made for my children which are 5 and 2 years old. It is a kids game where you have to break balloons using the car you drive. There are no lives or shots and it was even planned that there would be no game over. 

In recent months, the possibility of sending it to the Capacitor Party emerged and this changed the first idea a bit. Checkpoints were added and that made it possible to lose (game over) if you run out of time. Even so, the difficulty is low and it should be easy to finish the three levels that exist. 
 
The game was created by Guillermo Amat aka Dueteros. 
To start choose a car, a color and a character. Each vehicle has its own characteristics:

    The 4x4 is very slow, but it has the ability to jump very high and does better than the rest on oil spots.
    The Sport car has intermediate characteristics compared to the other two.
    The formula is very fast, jumps at low altitude and gets stuck in the oil.

212707.overview: An AMOS artillery game where the projectiles are cows. A two-player only game with a silly sense of humour. Note the cows will say hello to each other in mid-air. Avoid the mountains and any floating, evil penguins.

212708.overview: An Arkanoid style bat and ball game, created in AMOS by C. Hodges that was originally released to public domain in 1992, the 1.4 update was released on October 30, 1997. The game features what some would call sideways play as the bat is on the right side of the screen and the brick configuration is on the left, rather than the traditional top and bottom arrangement.

212710.overview: A nicely made game of Crazy 8's, similar to UNO with lots of user customization available. You can change sounds, music, cards, palette at any time during the game. You can change scoring options, player names, and locale, with the ability to have multiple player preferences. User selectable music, sounds and many languages supported.

212733.overview: Published by Markt & Technik in the Amiga Spielesammlung Band 2 compilation. A 2D single screen puzzler where you push shapes into holes. In order to finally create order again, you balance boxes in a basement that is much too narrow. Very easily?

212749.overview: A polish racing game where you can choose up to nine different rounds per race and up to 4 racers can play. In classic mode you don't get a point for the round if you crash.  Game can be played in Polish or English, and the graphics are very basic, but still great for parties. Saves best time overall.

213517.overview: A reimagined port of the 1986 original but with visuals inspired by Castlevania Chronicles and other non-8 bit titles in the series. The goal was to provide a playable and pure version of the original Castlevania but with an Amiga flavor. Not a port of the Sharp X68000 or PlayStation "Castlevania Chronicles" game, it only happens to use many level tiles and sprites from that game because it's a practical rendition of how OG Castlevania would look in 16-bit or 32-bit.

213630.overview: A single player collect'em up game by Dan of Pendle Europa. You start as the red car, the computer is green. Avoid the green car and pick up all the pellets. Once all the pellets have been gathered you go on to the next level.

213631.overview: A casino style fruit\slot machine by Simon R Smith. This is an accurate fruit machine simulator. Leave disk write enabled to ensure this machine "pays out" an overall minimum average of 80 percent. Hit return to insert 1 pound. Space to pull the handle. 12 or 3 to hold reels. C to cancel or collect. Backspace to insert money won.

213632.overview:
This is an Amiga port of Castle Danger - a board game made about 20 years ago by Matt Worden for the PC. All assets are taken from the original and converted to the Amiga format to give the game the same look and feel. I wrote the whole game code from scratch.
I also added something that the PC version lacked - single player mode. Writing it was the biggest challenge of it all and most time consuming. A new version was released that has an improved single player AI.  Castle Danger is a one or 2-player, turn-based strategy game. Each turn, a player gets to add another piece to their side of the board, move their pieces, and shoot cannonballs at their opponent. Who will hit the other's King first?

The game supports hotseat (2 players on the same computer), NetPlay (remote computers connected through the internet or other TCP/IP network), and play-by-email (through the game save/load functions).
 
The game board (shown below) consists of a 9-by-7 grid of squares. The middle column on the board is an impassible river. The Blue player's pieces will all be located on the left half of the board, and the Red player's pieces will all be located on the right half. The two wedge-shaped items in the middle outer squares (one blue, one red) are called "Portals" ... this is where new pieces will be introduced to the game. 
The King is the piece that needs to be protected throughout the game. Each player gets only one of these, and when it is hit by a cannonball, the game is over.

Wizards add moves for the player to use each turn. A player starts with 3 moves/turn, and gets an additional 3 moves/turn for every Wizard they have on the board.

Builders can add and remove Walls from the board. Since cannonballs cannot pass over Walls, Builders can be used to build up protection for the King (and the other pieces too).

Cannons fire cannonballs at the opponent. Wherever the cannonball lands, Fire is added to the game board, replacing whatever piece had been there. Cannonballs can fly over any piece on the board, except for Walls. The game is over when a King gets hit by a cannonball.

Walls are added to (and removed from) the game board by Builders. Walls provide protection from cannonballs.

Fire is left behind wherever a cannonball hits. The Fire lasts through just the opponent's turn, then disappears. Pieces cannot move onto a square that holds Fire.

213633.overview: A Rampart style game released in 1993 by Christopher Jennings and Chris Cooke where you build your castle and defend it with catapults!

213634.overview: An Amiga port of the vastly popular board game of checkers or droughts. In it, you can choose a one or two player game and the level of difficulty if playing against the machine. You can also show threats, forfeit moves, take moves back and swap sides for a better view from your opponent's perspective.

213635.overview: Cheop is an Egyptian themed platform game created by Michael Taupitz. It had multiple versions including the commonly found 2.0 version. The goal is to get the sequentially appearing vases while evading all the mummies. you can jump, push some blocks, and... that's it. The level design is a bit on the tricky side, as you can see, and there's a level editor included there... somewhere.

213637.overview: Chińczyk is a computer adaptation of an ancient Hindu board game called Pachisi. The game allows to play up to four human or computer players. Each player's objective is achieving the base by all four pawns before the opponents. Reaching the base requires making a full encirclement of the board. Pawn leaves the starting place after throwing 1 or 6 on the dice. Opponent pawn can't be overtaken, but it can be beaten after entering its field. Beaten pawn back to the starting point. The player may have any number of their pawns on the board at one time, but only one pawn may be moved with a single throw. Throwing a dice value higher than all pawns are eligible to move or lack of possibility of leaving the starting position (2-5 or blocked extraction point) means a loss of turn.

213639.overview:
A re-imagining of a game by Dr Hirudo, Chips is a challenging puzzler where you're trying to piece together a working Amiga computer by combining chips scattered all over the main board.

Controls: Joystick/Arrow Keys to Move / Navigate Menus

Fire/Enter to Punch / Select

ESC to Show in-game menu / Speed up score bonus

By standing next to a chip you can press Punch to send it flying in a straight line across the main board. Hitting a matching one will make it disappear. Stopping when finding a different one in its path. Look out! Chips (just like you) can move through the edges and reappear on the other side. If there's nothing in its path you'll get zapped! When the last two matching chips collide they change into a custom chip. You then have to combine them in a similar way to get a working Amiga.

213641.overview: A single screen remake of the 2 player-only dueling game. If you go off one side of the screen you loop around to the other. Weapon distance is fairly small so you will need to get in close and hopefully behind your victim...er opponent. Good luck and good shooting!

213642.overview: A thrilling car chase through a huge city by Darius Lorenc aka Lorenz released on Amiga Fun (Computec) Issue 5. A game for real game freaks! Strong graphics and lots of action make this super game a real hit!

213644.overview:
A little Frogger clone by the demogroup Rebels. Claude's Runner is a single player, keyboard controlled Frogger variant.

In this game he player has to move Claude from the bottom of the screen to the top across three lanes of very busy motorway. Once across the roads Claude disappears from top of the screen and reappears at the bottom with another set of roads to cross.

The layout of the roads is always horizontal but it changes with each screen. The game has sound but no high score table, once all lives have been exhausted the player is returned to the menu screen.

213646.overview: Push all the blocks to the red space to destroy them, push orange balls together to remove them, or push them at walls or blocks to destroy the walls or blocks. See how far you can get in the lowest number of moves. A game for one or two players by André Treptow. It was released in both a Freeware and a Shareware version. Push the numbered blocks together to clear them out and move to the next level.

213659.overview: An earlier form of this game was being played thousands of ears ago. It has since evolved into an enthralling game, in which chance and tactics go hand in hand. The object of the game is to be the first one to get all your pieces home and to move them outside the board. Barriers are set up on the way and double bets serve to heighten the tension. Once  you are engrossed in the game, you will quickly discover why the game has survived all these centuries.

213720.overview: A 5 card, draw poker style video poker, casino game from Late Storey.

213721.overview: Card Sharp V1.0 was published with OTHELLO on 17 Bit PD disk #2141. Card Sharp is a game, created by Wizz of Tower Software and released in 1992. It is a set of solitaire games including Klondike, King Albert, Calculation, Demon and Castle.

213722.overview:
A "Memory" game where you flip cards to find matching pairs. If the pairs don't match, the cards are flipped again, so that you must memorise the position of each card flipped in order to beat the computer (which doesn't have the kind of exact memory you'd expect of a computer).

During play, the computer chats along, commenting on how the game is going, bragging when it finds a pair and complementing your play style. A "peek" option will flash the cards for a few seconds so that you can refresh your memory — and your opponent's. Running in low resolution, the game is fully system friendly and comes with source code in C language.

213723.overview: Featured on Amiga Fun (Computec) 2/1990, game coding, graphics & sound by Ronald Mayer. it is a four reel slot\fruit machine with various betting lines.

213724.overview: A collection of solitaire games created by Martin Wilson. Games include: Pyramid, Golf, Klondike, Corners, Calculation, Canfield and an option to play the "Grand Tour". The game was released to public domain in 1992.

213725.overview: Video Poker is similar to poker machines in many countries, however it is unique in Australian pubs. I t involves playing poker and attempting to double your winnings. This version includes full sound and the ability to load your own sound files, it also saves the statistics for your review and viewing pleasure.

213738.overview: An elegant, single screen version of the classic board game Clue from Greg Pryor and released in 1986. Determine who killed Mr. Body, in which room and with what weapon based on the bits of information given, which help to rule out a portion of your options.

213740.overview: A space themed turn based, 2D strategy game, for one or two players created by Christian Mumenthaler and released in 1993. Like a mix of Civilization and Master of Orion with four levels of difficulty. This game is a precursor to Colonial Conquest II.

213741.overview: A board game strategy reworking XiangQi commonly known as Chinese Chess, which can be viewed in several different perspectives depending on your personal preferences. It is a fully featured game that will help you learn the game moves and strategy as you play. A very finished and enjoyable strategy experience that will test your ability to think ahead and counter your opponent for one or two players.

213742.overview: In this game, you will have to be quick thinking in how you can fit the colored pieces on the board. It was programmed at the time when these types of games were in fashion, such as Tetris, Columns, etc, and the language used was AMOS, thanks to the idea of ​​our esteemed Jose Heredia.

213744.overview: A Columns clone where you can only rotate through colors. It was created by Keith Johnson and released in 1992. The game features two game modes, and endurance game and an arcade style game.  The object of Colors is simply to form lines of four blocks or more of the same color. Pieces, which consist of 3 blocks are randomly picked and then descend, Tetris-style. The larger the lines you form, the more points you get.

213745.overview: In this puzzle and patterns game you try to alter the arrangement of blocks you've been given in order to match the setup on the right hand side of the screen in the fewest possible moves. Complexity increases as you solve levels as time given to solve the puzzle decreases.

213746.overview: A Snake\Worm style action game with puzzles created by Roberto Scacchetti and released in 2005.  You start as a snake of one color, but if you change color make sure to alter your eating style and only eat your current color. Add in mazes, the rapidly ticking time clock and the difficulty can increase very quickly! When you've removed all the blocks you move on to a harder level.

213747.overview: This is what puzzle games are all about - mad panic - move the paint through the maze to the containers at the bottom - you need to move the tunnels about to enable the paint to reach the bottom - this game will be frustrating. There are a set number of each color required in each of the bottom containers to move to the next, more difficult level.

213748.overview: The aim in this color matching puzzle game is to get as many points as possible without letting the balls get too high. Whenever there are three or more balls of the same color in a row, those balls disappear. The point count is as follows the number of balls squared. So 3 balls away is 9 points, 5 balls we is 25 points. But beware, there are different shades of color that must be matched. And different shapes only match with themselves.

213749.overview: Copper is an homage to Arkanoid, the objective of the game is to destroy all the bricks on the screen with the ball. Some bricks may take only one hit to disappear, others may take as many as 8 hits. Different bonuses pop up like viruses around the bricks if you hit them you will see the effect, some allowing remote control of the ball, others destroying all bricks in the path of the ball, giving your ship\vaus\bat a "lazer" or doubling your ball. These power ups only last about 20 seconds in many cases.

213750.overview: This MasterMind clone was published on the coverdisk of the August 1991 issue (#25) of Amiga Format, first released on July 11th, 1991. The computer will generate a four colour code, from a maximum of five different colours. Can you crack the code in less than TEN guesses and beat the computer.

213753.overview: Move one ball around the board to access the controls to move the blue ball around the same board to the X, then move yourself there to proceed to the next level. Don' leave the playing surface or cause the blue ball to leave the playing surface. Watch the timer! This game was released in Amiga Magazine 42 (Nov - Dec 1996) and came with a level editor to make your own games.

213754.overview: Move your joystick only to the right in order to run at the fastest speed as you race against an opponent or against your own best recorded time.

213755.overview: A game of strategy and reflexes by Joe Rumsey. A Pipe Dream clone where you need to avoid spilling any water for as long as possible. Use the mouse to place sections of pipe on the board so that the water has somewhere to flow. The water flows from the S (source) and can be sped up by hitting the F key. In this version cross pieces can be used with great safety, if there is pipe on the other side water will not flow through the unused ends.

213756.overview: Cricket Crazy is 2D sports Cricket game by Paul Dowers also released as International Cricket in 1992. Touting itself as the ultimate in cricket simulations, combining management and arcade action.

213757.overview: Destroy all the Croin Asteroids and eliminate the enemy ships you will meet within them. Every four stages or so you'll have to face and destroy an enemy mother-ship. In the subsequent stage you will need to pick up as many diamonds as possible before time runs out.

213758.overview: The aim of Cross Over is to collect all of the circles by moving your square over them and then moving the combined items to the nearest X. You must do all this within a given time limit. ON some level there are numbered tiles that can be used to help you reach normally impossible places, but be careful when you move these tiles as they can destroy each other. A 1 can hit a 2, 2 can hit a 3, 3 can hit a 4 a four can hit a 1.

213759.overview: Cubistix is a 3D Tetris game for 1 - 2 players. There are lots of different options for inputs and many stats about the game are shown.

213857.overview: Navigate the maze, use the switches to open passages, avoid the spectres and catch the green Gobblie. You only have three lives so be careful!

213888.overview:
CubeMaster is an arcade action game in the style of Asteroids. In the game, a CubeMaster is a combination of an athlete and an astronaut whose task it is to defeat wave after wave of CubeDrones. Like in Asteroids, the player moves his craft (the manned mobility unit) around a zero gravity environment where the player can use a thrust to move forward and a counter force to slow down as well as rotating left and right. The drones come in two sizes. Shooting the large ones will cause them to break into smaller ones. If the smaller drones are not destroyed quickly enough they will revert to the larger size again. The player's cannon builds up heat as it is used and when overheated it needs some time to cool down.

Drones of different colors have different abilities and if the player is not quick enough in shooting them down they will change. Among these are the yellow that when touched will make the player's controls all mixed up. Others include the blue ones that decreases the firing power, the red one that depletes the shield and the dark grey ones that when shot allow the player to pass through other drones. There is also the green drones, that doesn't change color, and that requires multiple shots to take down. In addition to the drones there are also other bad guys that try to get the player.

214097.overview: A remake of the popular game Jumpman Junior from the C64 version, so a much more basic layout, with the same levels from the Epyx original.

214783.overview: The David Addison games originally appeared on Fred Fish 28 (and 15 for his other original game set). This one, like the others was created in ABasiC and released to the public domain in 1985. This one is an implementation of Cribbage for the Amiga.

214784.overview: An implementation of "Cribbage" for the Amiga, running in no less than six windows on the Workbench screen. It plays against the computer with full muggins and bar rules. There are three difficulty levels and the game is entirely mouse-driven. Pressing the "help" key gives you hints on what hand to keep.

214873.overview: The third game in the series, following Kill Em All and Countdown to Extinction, it would be followed by Hangar 18. This adventure-shooter series is packed with 7 missions and tons of weapons. You are sick and are prepared for cryogenic sleep in 2025 as tensions between the superpowers is growing and Europe is uniting to throw the US off of European soil. You awake in Paris in the year 3655 in a time of heightened mental abilities but with the major cities in ruins from a great war between the superpowers and as resources became more limited. You are told the stories of the former wars and how your skills can help in their current battle, they need someone not sensitive to psychic attacks to fight for them and so you have been revived. Can you help them to finally achieve peace through superior use of firepower?

214897.overview: A Scorpion Engine created Action/Adventure/Platformer that doesn't just feature complex levels, but a story, enemies, big bosses and dangerous traps. Francis is waiting for his friends in the bar when disaster strikes! Some sort of magical catastrophe has befallen the town of Gorcester! No time to think! You’ll have to find your friends before setting off on an arduous journey to confront whoever, or whatever is responsible!

214899.overview: A game created by Johnny Acevedo and friends for Amiten Games. This is a space invaders clone with multiple weapons in a cyberpunk atmosphere. The Cyberpunk City of Night Bloom are invaded by the Aliens , Marc the Mercenary have work to do...

214901.overview: You can choose three difficulty levels, 2 score systems with or without timer, 11 games (Klondike, Quatro, Findit, Memory, Freecell, Pyramid, Spider, Hanoi, Golf, Canfield, Agnes), background colors, selection colors, play out of game music, choose cardsets and tunes, save your presets and make your own cardsets with this version. There are over 750 cardsets created for this game in circulation.

214902.overview: A non-AGA conversion of Klondike deluxe for all Amiga owners to use. Cardz retains one of the best features of Klondike Deluxe, i.e. the ability to load other card sets and dozens and dozens of high quality card sets were available for this game. The game was created by Paul Morley and released to public domain in 1995.

214903.overview: A freeware puzzle game created by Martin Kasprzik and released in 1994.

214920.overview: A new set of exclusive levels for CarVup, this stand-alone 2D platform, painter style game has more fun from the game you love! It was created by Core Design and released on the cover disk of The One magazine in 1990.

214922.overview: A French language version of the Risk board game with 3 to 6 players, created by Cyrille Guillaume and released in 1997.

214923.overview:
Federation is a strategy game, created by Gordon Miller that takes place in space. There are lots of different options and it is quite difficult. For advanced players only... 
 
The Galactic Federation welcomes you to the finest army in the galaxy. As a new recruit you will receive a brand new starship, 35000 cash advance and a lifetime of adventure.

214924.overview: A sequel to Gordon Miller's Federation, like the original Federation game, this is a strategy game, created by Gordon Miller that takes place in space. There are lots of different options and it is quite difficult. For advanced players only... The Galactic Federation welcomes you to the finest army in the galaxy. As a new recruit you will receive a brand new starship, 35000 cash advance and a lifetime of adventure.

214969.overview: A Dutch farming simulator slash vehicle avoidance game created by Herman Harmers, Cor De Vries and Richard van de Veen, known collectively as Video Computer Commericials and relased in 1989.

215006.overview: A top-down racing game which allows you to race C5's around a track, against a friend or computer or even on your own in time trial mode. Who needs fast formula 1 racing when you can race a three speed plastic C5 around the track? The game features a flat battery mode for 2 players only, and fastest lap/race times and championship tables are all automatically saved. A track editor is enclosed.

215062.overview: 2-Card Poker is played with a standard deck of 52-cards. No jokers or wildcards are used. Players are required to make an ante wager before seeing any cards. Once the bet is placed the dealer will deal four cards to each player and themselves. Players are playing against the dealer to settle all ante and bet wagers.

215084.overview:
A Taipei sytle Shanghai Mahjong solitaire game from Dirk Hoffmann (and Nikl Gunther?) of Delta Software, it was released in 1990 by DevWare. Captivating thinking and strategy game à la Shanghai; free pieces of the same appearance must be placed in pairs playing field must be cleared.  
 
China Challenge is quite similar to the well-known game Shanghai or Mahjong. The goal of China Challenge is to remove all pieces of the pile, known as the "Dragon," step by step. This dragon consists of 120 unique tiles, and you can only remove tiles when they match. It's highly addictive!

215104.overview: Co do grosza is an enhanced classic board monopoly game for up to five players. The main rules remain unchanged. Each round begins with rolling the dice. The players move around the board, buy, sell and pledge of real estate or invest in infrastructure. The game introduced all the classic fields, such as prison or train stations and a lot of new ones, such as random encounter or lotto lottery, as well as some new features, such as property stock exchange or bank loan. Full board encirclement ends up with Year summary - including a fee, taxes, expenses, account interest rates or repayment of loans.

215105.overview: Cylogic is a puzzle game, developed by Cybestyle and published by Amigo!, which was released in Europe in 1990.  It was released on issue 4 of Amigo!.

215106.overview:
Clever & Smart is an action game with puzzle elements, based on the Spanish comic book series Mortadelo y Filemón. The two protagonists are special agents and in this game they need to find Dr. Bakterius who was kidnapped by the competing agency OMA.

The main part of the game takes place on the city map which is shown from a top-down perspective (except persons, cars and trees). Here the protagonists need to explore the city and its sewers to find hints on Bakterius' location. However, there are many locations where Clever & Smart need to have certain items in their possession to proceed. For example to enter some houses Clever needs to use one of his trademark disguises or in the sewer they can tap telephone phone line with the right tools.

Another important resource is money which is used to buy items, disguises and food. The latter is essential for survival because a hunger value constantly rises when the heroes don't eat. Money is either earned by illegal activities like burglary or forging checks or by playing mini games like flipping coins or a snail race (Clever participating himself in disguise).

215157.overview: A war strategy game from Gyrus Software Group, released in 1992. The title sequence seems intended to invoke Command & Conquer but gameplay feels a bit more like Civilization with a focus on the fighting aspects of the game.

215158.overview:
Critical Hit is a highly detailed fantasy combat game, which re-creates tabletop war gaming on the Amiga. It features a complex and accurate combat system, in which the skills, equipment, health and injuries of individual soldiers are traced. Many real and fantastic creatures are included, each with their own skills, psychology profiles and leadership characteristics.  
  
Complete campaigns may be waged, which consist of series of individual battles. The result of the battles determines the flow of the campaign. Battles are depicted on stunning three dimensional landscapes, and a wide variety of fantasy combat figures and scenery is utilized.

The Unregistered Shareware version runs on 1MB machines, and includes a single campaign, “Goblin”. This version does not include any music, and uses only some of the available features of Critical Hit. 
 
Full version 1.2 is now available for free (requires 1.5MB RAM). I cannot guarantee support for free copies of Critical Hit.

215159.overview: It is a race against time to get all the stars! When you start the slider moving it will go until stopped. Move around your blockers so that you can slide them around and pick all the stars up in time without getting off track.

215472.overview: Like Frogger with a twist - the number of lanes increases with each level. Supports two players. Password free by permission of author. This is Croaker by Brian Grier from 1993. You start with your Frog at the bottom of the screen, and your task is to get it into one of the spaces at the top of the screen. While this may sound easy, You have to cross a road, which as levels progress, will get busier, and busier with traffic, making this more and more difficult. When you get to the central part, which you may think is safe, a Snake can sometimes appear and it randomly moves across the screen, which you must avoid, otherwise it will cost you a Frog. Once the central pathway has been passed, it is onto the logs, where you will navigate them without falling into the cold harsh water, which will cost you a life. Then finally on the last log, it is your last jump to freedom, which you must time well, otherwise you will hit your head on the wall, which will cost you a life. There is some pretty nice Croaky Title Screen music, and in-game you have Croaky sounds as your Frog moves around, as well as traffic noises, all the sounds are really nicely done, and are pleasant to listen to.

215479.overview: Cesta Tmou, which means, "a path through the dark",  is an Adventure text game in czech language. It's the sequel to Drsná Cesta. The second part of the trilogy of text adventures, whose creator is Jan Burian alias Utopia from the group Torture. This trilogy of text games consists of three parts called Rough Road, Dark Road and Dead Road.

215497.overview: The Curse of Rabenstein is the new graphic adventure from Stefan Vogt, the author of the acclaimed Hibernated interactive fiction series. It is the first release from Puddle Soft, a collective formed by members of Pond and with the mission of creating new games for the classic 8-bit and 16-bit home computers of the 80s. The Curse of Rabenstein is following the paths of the legendary adventures from Level 9, but it tries to meet modern gaming expectations, so that the most sophisticated genre back from the day transforms into a contemporary homage.

216317.overview: Chess 2.0 is an updated Amiga port of the Stanback Chess Program. In contrast to the 1.0 port, this version has a fully mouse-driven graphical interface, while retaining the original SCP chess engine. Each game starts with setting the chess timer. Since the computer uses all the time alloted to calculate as many moves as possible, fast players are usually favoured over slow-thinking ones. Games can be saved and loaded, the board can be flipped and players can change sides. The colours of the board and pieces may be changed, and there is online help. The program may give hints, there is an "undo" function and the board may be manipulated, removing or adding pieces. The list of moves may be saved to disk or viewed on-screen, and there is a bank of game openings supplied.

217257.overview: An unfinished open source shooter created for the Amiga Blitz Basic Game Jam in 2022. In it, you need to stop all the nasty Caps from hurting your 68000 CPU!

217266.overview: Welcome to Chaos Arena! Pit yourself against seasoned warriors in the most frantic duel to date! Every warrior looks the same, so your first challenge is to figure out who's who. The only way to defeat others is to push them out of arena with your attacks, but beware - your fierceful strikes may also push you into abyss. Also, the arena constantly crumbles, so no hiding around! The last man standing wins.

217463.overview:
A version of the Othello board game by Exodus-Soft and released by King Soft (Robtek) and later in International Arcade Action and the Amiga Stars Collection compilations. It was coded in AmigaBASIC and released in UK and Australia and while known as Championship Othello, it only said Othello on the Robtek retail box. The OziSoft Amiga Stars Collection had the Championship Othello name. 
 
Othello is an exciting board game played against the computer or another person on a 8 x 8 grid. The idea is to try and place your piece so that it outflanks your opponent creating a horizontal, vertical or diagonal run of opposing pieces, making them yours. Player with the most pieces 'WINS'.

217537.overview: Connect is a classic logic game. The game is inspired by Hashiwokakero logic puzzles. Chips are placed on a circuit board and the player has to place connections between them.

218101.overview: It's time for even more Christmas goodness, as if you have a Commodore Amiga at hand or an emulator installed, you might like to play this fun for all the family game of Crimbo by Spud. An unofficial ZX Spectrum to Amiga conversion of the game "Crimbo" by Little Shop of Pixles. Here is what Spud says about this brand new game of Crimbo for the Amiga 500 1.5MB and above : "I did a simple and very unofficial ZX Spectrum to Amiga conversion of the game "Crimbo" by Little Shop of Pixles. Somewhat rushed and unoptimized in an attempt to get it out before Christmas because who wants to play a Christmas themed game after that? There are one or two things missing, maybe they'll be added for next yea, but I know it is simple both graphically and in terms of game play so I hope you enjoy! Instructions: go collect the gifts the nasty elves have stolen from Santa, etc etc. Controls are left right and fire for jump on the joystick".

219375.overview: Člověče, nezlob se! is a Czech public domain\freeware game created by Karel Klaizner and Marian Brngál, collectively known as the Methanoids and released in 1995 with releases for DOS and the Atari ST as well as the Amiga. This puzzle game also goes by the name Ludo or  "Mensch, ärgere dich nicht".

219377.overview: A board game style game by Aristosoft based on the 1989 award winning board game 'Cafe International'.

220122.overview: Become the president of a prestigious club, its renowned coach, its most talented player! Buy one of 32 top European clubs and raise big money from grants, sponsors and TV rights. Show initiative, intelligence and nerve! Transfer star players to your club who will bring you additional advantages during the matches. To win on the pitch, you have to behave exactly as in reality and follow as closely as possible the spirit and rules of modern football. Infinite possibilities of movements and tactical combinations. In the senior version, complete management of faults: touch, corner, offside, free kick, expulsion, penalty... This exciting simulation plunges you into the exciting atmosphere of major international competitions and will make you experience

418307.overview: One-of-a-kind German business simulation around the illegal cracking, copying and selling of software. Shipped as number 12-01 of the Nordlicht software series. It holds some historical value to show what the Amiga market was like in 1993.

418315.overview: A shooter created with the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit. Released as part of the Nordlicht Spiele Pack 3. Game features baddies with Atari symbols and reworked sprites from Space Invaders and power ups with Commodore branding and symbols. The various waves of attackers come from above, while you have to shoot down the invaders with your spaceship at the bottom of the picture.

418324.overview:
The Child Murderer is a shareware text and graphics adventure game designed for the beginning level player. The player takes the role of Charles Browning, personal servant to Robert Harris a rich businessman living in Victorian London. You are blamed for a murder you did not commit, and must both evade your captors and find the real killer.

The text parser uses small Verb / Noun sentences, such as Talk to the woman, or Use the candle. In addition a menu of common commands and keystroke shortcuts is displayed in most locations and key objects in the game are preceded with the term, Visible Objects.

418331.overview: Ciach-Bach is a simple three educational games set for kids. The first game is a 3x3 grid puzzle, featuring a total of ten pictures. The second one allows to practice playing on cymbals\xylaphone (includes recording possibility) and the last one is a sixteen colors cut & paste, sticker fun subgame.

418371.overview: In this shareware platformer release, you control a bull intent on smashing all the precious china while the shop owner drops bombs from the ceiling in an attempt to stop you.

418390.overview: Controlling a mouse with the joystick, you collect cheese and try to avoid being eaten by the cat. The cat can be stunned if you manage to lure him into a mouse trap, but be careful hitting any traps yourself. It was commercially released as part of the AMIGA MEGA PAK software compilation.

418398.overview: Navigate to the other side of the cave without touching the walls or being touched by the rapidly moving and sometimes mercurial cave denizens. A freeware game from Peter Whitlock.

418406.overview: A single player Shoot'em Up made with the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit by J. Carp and released in 1995. It was released shortly after the bankruptcy of Commodore and is intended to send a final message to the company's failed executives. You play as the Amiga Boing Ball and make your final stand against Commodore's industry competitors. Enemies include the then-current logos of Microsoft, IBM, Apple, and Intel, which you fire the Workbench default cursor at. The level backgrounds are an Amiga mainboard with microchips, the Amiga Workbench, CompUSA shops, and a literal interpretation of the Internet as the information superhighway. At certain points, you encounter the Amiga Software Failure screen with red text on black and get attacked by what appears to be virus-infected disks. The last level of the game is truly something special.

418427.overview: Game written exclusively for use with the Golem light gun, but there are versions hacked so it can be played with a mouse.  You get five levels with moving obstacles to shoot at. One thing that really stands out for this game are  the backgrounds: That is some excellent pixel art.

418432.overview: A game originally released as a shareware RPG adventure game, this game by Peter Gage was eventually and ominously available on Fred Fish Disk 666.

418442.overview:
Cave Story is a metroidvania platformer with the amnesiac soldier Quote finding a city of rabbits called Mimigas. The Mimigas are preyed on by an evil doctor, who kidnaps them for his evil experiments. They still remember Arthur, a hero from their past and others are awaiting for the return of Dragons. The soldier soon falls in with Sue, a stranger to the Mimigas, but the only one who seems to know about the Dragon Eggs. Unfortunately the doctor wants her next.

The game closely resembles a NES platformer with a distinct 8-bit style and fast gameplay. The main character collects weapons (blade, bubbler, fireball, machine gun, nemesis, (super) missile launcher, polar star, snake, and spur) that can be leveled up three times. There are also health capsules to increase his life bar. There is a variety of jumping puzzles and boss battles to challenge players as they explore the game.

418657.overview: A crossword puzzle game created by Greg Abernethy and Martin Fitzgibbons of Rush Software in Australia and published by the same starting in 1993.

418666.overview: A homebrew single player\single car racing game where you race around the track and try to best your time. The game is contained on Fred Fish disk 0336.

418700.overview: A multi-directionally scrolling shooter.  In the two player mode one player controls the ship and the other controls the aiming and shooting. The two player mode can be used by a single player too by using a controller and keyboard simultaneously which gives more control to the aiming process. The game was released to the public in the beginning of 2018 by Avesoft founder Jyrki Kummola at the birthday party of the Finnish game museum where the finnish game/digital media preservation group Kasettilamerit was present. Both Jyrki Kummola and the makers of the game have given their permission that it can now be freely distributed.

418776.overview:
30 years on... Lead the next generation of CyberPunks on even more dangerous missions into space and beyond.

Engage in battle against relentless swarms of alien creatures with your team of cyber marines and return order to a chaotic planetary system.

418777.overview: The fourth episode of the popular Commander Keep saga, ported to the Amiga by BSzili in 2016 and based on the Reflection Keen port by NY00123.

418872.overview:
The game is a very simple FPS before Wof3D, consisting of twenty levels that are quite challenging but not impossible. Ported from DOS without license, this game credits the original id Software as developers for this release. Just like the original, you are a mage descending into the dungeons of Grelminar the Lich, in order to kill him and save one guy named Nemesis.

Catacomb 3-D is a simple fantasy first-person shooter game. To get to Grelminar, you have to complete several maze-like levels. Your sole weapon is a fireball spell, which can be used an unlimited number of times and can be charged up to cause more damage. You can also find one-time use items: bolts and nukes. A bolt launches several fireballs in a machine-gun fashion, while a nuke launches a ring of fireballs in all directions.

The various enemies (such as orcs or trolls) that you meet while exploring are the main target for those fireballs. However, you can also destroy whole sections of walls, which is often necessary to complete the level.

Items you can find include (apart from bolts and nukes) healing potions, keys to open doors, and scrolls that provide hints.

There isn't an overhead map in the game, but you have a compass to guide you. What's more, various areas of the map have specific names displayed at the bottom of the screen, making it a bit easier to navigate.

418953.overview: Arcade version of Outrun on the Amiga

419538.overview: "Chopper Duel is something you have been waiting for the last two months... And here it is! The ultimate two-player air combat game! With a friend, you will have several sleepless nights with Chopper Duel!"

419736.overview: Amiga Public Domain RPG involving casting spell and the balance of power in a single screen, top-down dueling style game. This is the game that started it all. Created by James Conwell (ChaosLord), the devoted Amiga coder/hobbyist, who died in July 2016 after a long battle with Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy, this game would evolve into several games including 2001's, Chaos: Wizard War II and eventually the epic Total Chaos: Battle At The Frontier Of Time from 2003. This was the first and the version that played best on the original A500 system, while later games were aimed at the A1200 and A3000 computer systems.

420709.overview: Most versions found are a very limited demo version where there are no cities, dungeons, functional battles, missions or purpose. All it has is wilderness, character sheets and inventory routines.

420722.overview: A wizardly caravan mode shmup, by Peter & Gordon Mackay. Made for AmiGameJam 2022. Requires an Amiga 1200 or higher.

420856.overview: A single player collect'em up game where you act as a kind of Pac-Man collecting up the dots. The enemies act in certain repeatable ways and the number of them and the way they react changes as you increase in levels.

420857.overview: A cross-country road race in your supercar, see how fast you can get through all the tracks as you win your way across the nation from New York to San Francisco.

420860.overview: An overhead racing game preview by Menato Denny from 1995. The demo appears to just support a single user.

420861.overview: A shareware puzzle game from Pete W. Storonskij, released in 1994. Conundrum 2.0 is an abstract hexagonal based board game, wher the object is to negate all of the colored tiles by placing them next to each other. This game was inspired by those hexagonal floor tiles you find on restroom floors. Once you start you have 10 seconds to place a tile, each tile ranges from 1 to 10, having its own color configuration. The number on the tile is the number of negations that must be done on it. Tiles are negated by placing them side by side. The game starts with six negations per tile and can be negated from any adjacent position. The number of tile types starts slowly to allow you to understand the game play. You are given tiles and exploding tiles to play with.

420906.overview: ClassicZoo is a fork of ZZT by Adrian “asie” Siekierka, started in late 2020 and initially released in March 2021. Its goal is to improve the ZZT experience while sticking close to the original engine's feel and keeping full compatibility.

420967.overview: Choose from knight, archer, mage or monk to explore the dangerous monster-filled castle, or get a group and hit the dungeons with all four.  You'll need all the friends and all the luck you have to survive.

421000.overview: Written with both Backbone and AMOS this freeware 2016 demo game is something like Alien Breed. Teleport down and explore the cratered hell-scape. Shoot the enemy soldiers or evade and pick up healing and power ups. Push buttons to open doors and really explore the space.

421014.overview: Rolling demo of the game, not playable, but worth a watch.  Chancellor Jagoo from Murdrum Planet wants to pay you millions but don't ask too many questions and you must teleport immediately, this could be trouble.  Crimetown Depths is set on a planet ruled by a despot, where one of the futuristic megacities is now inexorably controlled by crime, so much so that it is nicknamed "Crimetown". The player plays as one of the mercenaries hired to clean up the city. Crimetown has vertical development, a heterogeneous alien population and high-tech structures, but in a dangerous state of decay. The mercenary would have to reach the deepest levels of the city to ferret out the sources of corruption.

421015.overview:
ChaosCastle is a simple shoot-em-up game: just destroy everything without
getting killed yourself. By collecting falling coins and various bonuses,
you'll get access to zones with many scrolling levels. You'll meat dangers
of any kind, mineral, vegetal and animal as well as fights against monsters.
Hidden items will allow you to use additional weapons and to increase
their power.

421196.overview: The programmer of this game launched a legal action against Rockstar North for alleged copyright violation due to the similarity of Grand Theft Auto to Crime Inc. and the fact that he had given them a demo of the game for consideration. A top down gangster themed game that was never finished.

421200.overview: A platforming tech demo from alpine9000 released in 2017, from the creators of Blocky Skies. This demo which they call Climby Skies is a brilliant showcase that shows their new Amiga game engine that runs with 32 colors at the same time and at a speed of 50FPS on an unexpanded Amiga 500! Brilliant!

421246.overview: Techdemo of our upcoming game, still buggy and unoptimized...

421470.overview: A connect four game for two players written by Chris Benton and released as shareware in 1992.

421544.overview:
Guide King Olof through the dungeon beneath the castle in search of evil prince Egnor in order to defeat him and regain the throne. Control is via the mouse. Selecting the appropriate icons in the border and using objects, fighting etc. in the main window. Clicking with the left mouse button on the directional arrows moves Olof in the appropriate direction (forward - walk forward, right - rotate right etc.) Also in the border is Olofs energy bar. The marker shows the energy, which goes down when Olof is hit. The compass next to the directional arrows shows the direction in which Olof is facing.
The bottom row of icons are the action icons these are selected using the right Mouse button and cancelled using the left mouse button.

The top row of icons are the item icons (these are empty to start with). As you collect items throughout the game their icons will appear in these boxes. These may also be selected and cancelled using the same method as the action icons.

Published in Software 2000 Volume 1 SET 2 CD 2.

421549.overview: Written as an umpire using the Napoleonic Wargame System and written in Hisoft Basic this game\utility by Ashley Sear was released as public domain in 1992.

421553.overview: Released as part of the Mega Games PD 2.2 collection and as part of an early Fish Disk compilation, this is a parser based text adventure by James Fox, created in 1990. Beautiful graphic adventure from 12th century England at the time of Robin Hood. Mouse-controlled operation; easy level of difficulty.

421554.overview:
An unauthorized remake of the classic early stealth shooter (which inspired the Wolfenstein FPS series). In this game, the player takes control of a lone prisoner who has been taking captive in a large castle occupied by the Nazis. Getting out of the cell and picking up a weapon is just the beginning; the ultimate goal is to acquire the war plans of the Nazis, and escape from Castle Wolfenstein alive.

Castle Wolfenstein is notable for being one of the earliest games that incorporated stealth-based gameplay mechanics. The player navigates the hero through the top-down corridors and rooms of the castle. The main gameplay challenge lies in dealing with the guards who patrol the castle and will be alerted to any noise made by the player. It is possible to shoot the guards, but the ammunition in the game is scarce, and some guards are very hard to kill, so the preferred course of action is moving without being noticed. If the player surprises a guard with a gun drawn, the guard will surrender, and the player will be able to frisk him for valuable items.

The player should also search the treasure chests scattered across the castle. Some of them contain war plans, which are essential for winning the game; others have useful items, such as bullets, grenades, bulletproof vests, and guard uniforms. The uniforms can be worn for disguise; however, higher-ranked SS guards will be able to recognize the intruder. Chests might also contain food and beverage; imbibing alcohol will result in a temporary loss of aim and balance for the player character.

421561.overview: Attempt to escape the maze of twisty turning passages. Pick your tools and and use the right equipment at the right time.

421571.overview:
A shareware release where you must collect all the fruit, as in the Dugger game.  Charlie Chatterbox is based on the old Spectrum game Splat!  by
Incentive Software the only major difference being that Splat! scrolled the screen in a semi-random way whereas 'Charlie' follows a set route.  The idea is to eat as many of the apples as possible whilst avoiding getting trapped behind walls as the screen scrolls. The only way you can die is to be forced into one of the sides of the playing area.  ** SHAREWARE ** 
 
This was released as shareware on the 17-Bit Software disk 3275.

421575.overview: A text-based space strategy game written in C by Carl Edman in 1990.

421577.overview: A Mastermind type game for one, created by Derek Piper and released as shareware in 1994.

421640.overview: A freeware AMOS game created by JIP Soft (Joona Palaste) in 1996. In it you must activate the charges and destroy the skulls before they discharge.

421657.overview: A one or two player, freeware color matching AMOS game from Claire Warner and Simon Hadley released in 1993.

421678.overview: Guide Cutesy the bear through 10 levels in the garden eliminate the baddies that threaten it in this colorful platformer by J. Monday from 1991. Bump the baddies from below and kick them off the platform remove them from the garden patch. Collect the snacks before clearing the last baddie gives a bonus snack screen! Each level is timed, so don't waste a precious second.

421683.overview:
Crillion is similar to Breakout except there is no paddle and the player controls the ball directly. The ball always bounces up and down and the player only controls its horizontal movement. When the ball hits a block of the same color it will dissolve. The ball can change color when hitting a color changer blocks, marked with an asterisk. The object of the game is to clear all blocks while avoiding the skull blocks.

When the player hits a skull block, a life is lost and the level restarts, resetting any progress made so far in that level. There also are unbreakable walls and slider blocks. The slider blocks can only be moved around when the ball has the same color. The Amiga version was to Amiga and later to PC using the version released by the original author, Oliver Kirwa,  to the Markt & Technique publication Happy Computer in July of 1988 as a type in game.

422512.overview: An educational art game by Computras International sold as Licenceware in 1990 to schools and educational programs. In this one you can use the computer to color in various pictures and images.

422516.overview: A program to help you create your own crosswords, give the word list and allow the program to craft the challenge with you!

422519.overview: In "Crossfire II" you play the role of Karsten, a fighter pilot of the rebels. A wide range of missions awaits you, ranging from escort, defense to large battles in an armada of ships. These missions tell an extensive story with several surprising turns that take you to the strangest places of the known universe.

422866.overview: An AMOS based action puzzle based on Boulderdash by Galaxya Software released in 1998. You get a free life after 10000 points. For some reason the third is the easiest in the set of puzzles.

422867.overview: A difficult homebrew Boulderdash clone created by Galaxya Software in 1993 which spawned several sequels. For each 10,000 points you get one additional life, but this is only shown at the end of the cave or when you die.

422870.overview: An AMOS based action puzzle based on Boulderdash by Galaxya Software released in 1994. You get a free life after 10000 points and you will need it. It has one precursor game and one sequel.

422871.overview: A one to three player puzzle game published as a cover disk in an Italian game magazine.

422893.overview: A well designed homebrew SEUCK based game by Cellar Software released in 1989. Feels like a zoomed in version of commando with more blood and where water kills you. There are also mines to avoid and medals and other supplies to pick up.

422916.overview: A realtime strategy game like dune 2 created by Jeppe Nielsen and released in the November 1999 Amiga Format CD #45. The game is intended to support 4 players.

422949.overview: A freeware worm style action game from Infect, created in 1994 using Blitz BASIC.

422951.overview: A freeware Blitz BASIC created shooter by Cyberware in 1997.

422961.overview: An AmigaBASIC single player pinball game created in 1989. Source code was distributed with the game.

422967.overview:
A PD game by Richard Reed, released as part of the Assassins Disk 134 and as a coverdisk on CU Amiga December of 1991. This fascinating and original strategy game places up to four players in an electrical arena where the object is to drain your opponents' power until they die. The game is played on a grid upon which a variety of electrical components can be placed, the most basic of which is a circuit. To wipe out the opposition you'll need to build a network which enables your Runners to reach them. 

The game is played in three phases: the action phase when new pieces are played: the movement phase when Grid-runners are moved and switches are opened and shut; and the power-up phase where players regain crucial energy according to the extent of their network. 

Due to the size of the instructions, we're unable to give you a full player's guide here, but if you use the PPMore option on disk 23, you can load the instructions from disk 22. They're in the 'Docs' directory of the disk, along with complete instructions for many of the other games. Version 1.4 of this game was also released on DevWare FunDisk 024 Strategy Games as Circuit Wars.

422976.overview: A 1993 AMOS based shareware quiz game by Paul Ciulla. There are two versions of this game, a free preview version and the full shareware version. The full version appears to allow multiple players via modem or cable connection.

422983.overview: A two-player freeware game from VSC Productions, made in 1994 using the SEUCK engine.

423015.overview: An AMOS based shareware puzzle game released  in 1996. There were two versions of this game, a demo and the full shareware version. Full source code came with the full version. Cantaloupe is an addictive tile-based puzzle/path-finding game.  It's based on an original C64 PD game, 'Sensitive', but a few extra tiles have been added.  Go on, try it: you might even like it. Intended for use on an A1200.

423085.overview: A 1995 freeware Czech text adventure written in AMOS by Roman Software. As King Jára, get back to your castle.

423087.overview: A bird's eye view, single player Roguelike. It is based off of an early mainframe game and was created and published by The Software Distillery in 1987 with 12 version updates being made. The game is one of the first Roguelikes (RPG dungeon crawls with top-down or isometric graphics and a high degree of randomization; Rogue or Nethack are examples) with a wilderness and more than one dungeon. In this game, you are searching the Caverns of Larn for a cure for your daughter's strange disease. The game world is presented entirely with ASCII text characters.

423088.overview: With features like a Dictionary you can use to check words and the ability to add words to your dictionary this will allow you to create puzzles of multiple sizes and even resize an existing puzzle and renumber as needed, this can help you make customized puzzles for any audience or occasion. Published by Polyglot Software in 1990.

423149.overview: A one or two player version of Centipede for the Amiga, created as freeware by Glen Lewis in 1989. Centipede is a simple clone of the arcade hit of the same name. Centipede moves from the top of the screen from the left side to the right, moving downward each time when contact with the fungus. Hitting any part of the Centipede transform that particular body segment into a mushroom. The player may move up and down in the limited forest area. Meeting with centipede ends the game. Randomly a spider appears. The spider moves in an irregular manner, distracting from the main objective.

423522.overview:
The Dungeons of Moria, usually referred to as simply Moria, is a computer game inspired by J. R. R. Tolkien's novel The Lord of the Rings. The objective of the game is to dive deep into the Mines of Moria and kill the Balrog. Moria, along with Hack (1984) and Larn (1986), is considered to be the first roguelike game, and the first to include a town level.  This game is a CWM Version created from this wellspring. CWM coding was done by Thomas Davies and Juha Niemimaki, who are somewhat hidden in the title screen but all in the name of full attribution to the work that had gone before. CWM Moria is an Amiga port of Umoria by Thomas H. Davies based on Umoria, the current version on aminet is from 1994, and is based on Umoria 5.5.2, the newest version, but Amiga CWM versions started much earlier.  
 
CWM Moria is open sourced with source code easily available.

423533.overview: Chánov is a homebrew text adventure game written in AMOS BASIC from Crudesys in 2008. It is the story of how a handsome young man came to Roma love. The choices you make will impact how the adventure flows and open up different avenues for the story to follow.

423558.overview: A shareware game written by Unicorn Systems in 1990 following the idea created by Dewdney where hostile programs engage in a battle of bits. It is a programming game in which two programs run in a simulated computer with the goal of terminating opponent. Once the game is started the player can watch the code overwriting all the memory.

423568.overview: Cesta bojovnika is The Way of the Warrior in Czech, a brutally militaristic text adventure by Kamil Blažek.

423650.overview:
"Chain Reaction" is a clever strategy game for one or two players. Whether you play against the computer or another human, the objective is the same: to eliminate all of your opponent's bomb-shaped pieces from the field of play. The game is played on a 6 X 6 grid of squares, and the players alternate turns, placing one bomb in a square on each turn.

The results of a move depend on how many bombs are already in the chosen square and adjacent squares. Whenever any square reaches "critical mass," it explodes and sends its bombs into neighboring squares. If those squares are already loaded to capacity, they explode too, creating a chain reaction that can engulf a large area of the board.

423658.overview:
The word ‘Chesmayne’ is taken from the French and means ‘Chess Company’. It is a contest of skill for two people and is played on a board marked with a lattice of cells of contrasting colour, which varies according to the size of the board chosen for play.

  Players in turn place a major or minor piece on one of the vacant or occupied cells with the object of capturing hostile pieces. The game (normally) ends when one King has been checkmated. This Amiga version by Raymond Reid and has many different games and challenges to explore and learn from. There is even a chess dictionary.

423664.overview: Chinese Checkers is a digital version of the popular German board game originally known as Stern-Halma, this freeware version is by Vidhyanath Rao and came out in 1990. The objective is to be the first player to move a group of 10 pieces to the opposite side of a star-shaped board; pieces can either be moved a single space, or 'jumped' over adjacent pieces.

423668.overview: A single player shareware version of Asteroids from John Harris in 1986. Shoot the asteroids, which will break up into smaller asteroids that are inherently more difficult to shoot. Once you clear all the asteroids you get a new set, with a slightly more difficult amount, speed and so forth.

423670.overview: Schiaccia Muri otherwise known as Crazy Wall is a bat and ball game like Breakout or Arkanoid where you must maneuver the bat under the ball to keep the ball in play and knocking out the bricks above until you have cleared all of them on the screen to move to the next level of play. This game was made by System-A software and released as freeware in 1990.

423675.overview: A puzzle game released as freeware from Dr Strange in 1992. Trace connections and items on the motherboard to repair and improve it in the quickest time.

423676.overview:
In Cubic you have to destroy the rows of blocks that slide down towards you by wiping out similar blocks.
