You have extras at your disposal, such as the bomb to destroy several blocks at once, or the universal block, which wipes out all the others. Sound effects, or on request give the fun the finishing touch. 
 
Released individually and as part of the Intelligent Fun game pack along with Tygard.

423782.overview: Explore the periodic table and all the elements withing, in Polish, with this game by Olaf Kostarczyn that was released by Alderan in 1992.  Contains messages in the field of inorganic chemistry. In the graphic form, all information from the Mendeleev Board, as well as information from the field of quantum mechanics.

423985.overview: Colotris is a Tetris variant. Each falling block is made of three colored squares, which order may be modified while descending to the bottom of the well. The combination of three squares of the same color (vertically or horizontally) causes their removal from the board. In addition to the blocks, bombs and stones may fall from the top. The second one remains on the board, the first one blow out the stones and a few adjacent blocks.

424335.overview: An unfinished Polish platform game created by Sławomir 'Korin' Jurałowicz in 2015.

442415.overview: A train management simulation game from the stalwarts of the genre, Ashley Greenup. In it you control the heart of the incredibly complex and busy Charing Cross station. You must make the trains run on time and get the freight safely to the proper destinations.

443929.overview:
A German-language, 4 player strategy game from Harald Paelzer, released in 1991 as OASE stock no. 143. 
Asar was once a thriving planet. But now he is in danger of falling victim to a catastrophe. It's high time for you and your research team to look for a place to stay for the residents of Asar on other worlds. 

To do this, equip your space fleet (how about a nice spoiler? Lower it? No problem!) and set off on an intergalactic journey in search of the right place. You have to conduct research, build atmospheres and trade on various planets. However, all sorts of space creatures are out to get you. So be careful! 

All 1-4 players also have a life of their own in the game. So they can trade with each other or fight each other. COLO-QUEST is a wonderful adventure game for strategy fans who appreciate biting humor.

443930.overview: CYBEXION is THE new addictive game. Various labyrinths have to be cleared by skillfully moving stones. However, your task is repeatedly hindered by many extras. A. Tactics game with a twist not just for puzzle fans and against the clock. Over 100 levels with password system, high scores.

445053.overview:
A Dutch-language one or 2 player word and letter puzzle game where you need to figure out the longest possible word from a list of given letters and then make the mental calculation using the numbers given to get to the result indicated. The game was based on a very popular and long running TV game show in many countries. 
 
 So you might get the number 683 and the numbers shown to use are 3, 8, 8, 100, 10 and 6. From there you need to determine that (6x100)+(8x10)+3 gets you 683. For the longest word section: In this test, the two candidates will take turns choosing the number of vowels they wish to have in the letter draw. 10 letters are then drawn randomly. The goal is to find the longest possible word using the letters that have been drawn, thus approaching the principle of the anagram.

446266.overview: Charlie Chimp is a platform game, which was released in Europe in 1993, updated and re-released in this 1996 version. Charlie Chimp won a AMOS game-competition. In it, you are Charlie, a chimp (surprise surprise!) and you have to walk around the levels changing the colour of all the platforms. There are all sorts of enemies walking around who try to stop you in your quest, but you can hit them with a tennis racket. There is a time limit and when you take too long, an evil big enemy appears who will try to stop you. The updated version was also released as an Amiga Action coverdisk.

448100.overview: An unfinished DOOM-like game from Primal (Nicolai Nyberg and crew) that was distributed in 1996. Not technically a shooter, as no shooting was yet available. Your tasks essentially boil down to searching the smoothly scrolling hallways for all the objects in them, finding weapons and keys, opening gates and giving the evil eye to enemies that occasionally march past.

448115.overview: CrossCircuit by David Wright is an action logic game that calls for fast thinking and fast reflexes. Equipped with a mobile electromagnet, your job is to grab various shaped connectors and drop them in place, forming a complete circuit across the screen. CrossCircuit is played with a joystick in port 2 or the keyboard. There are 8 levels of play. Plus the connectors on the left side of the screen to those on the right. If you complete all 8 levels, it goes to level 6 except with more plugs to connect and more difficult to reach.

448148.overview: Color Mania is a 1991 puzzle game written by Norbert Ossenkopp and published by Nosami. Colormania is simply everything about a 9-color cube with 144 stones, and is like a flattened version of a Rubic's cube. This can be twisted on all 4 sides in each row - so 48 ways... After you choose the level and up and press the start, the Amiga twists the dice. Now you need to bring it back to normal. Restore take back all player moves, resetting the cube puzzle. Buzzing show solution.

448150.overview: Clunk Click is a automotive based shooter/party game for up to 4 players. It was created with AMOS and originally released as a demo. This plays like a game of tag in a car. It appears to have been inspired by the cover of Amiga Power #53, but it was not released until 2 years later.

448319.overview:
The starship Equinox is under attack from Stormlord and his robotic minions, the Exolons! You’re the crew’s only hope. Take your Samurai-1 fighter, find Captain Solomon’s Key, clear the decks of evil robots, and save the Equinox from certain destruction!

Cecconoid is an 8-bit inspired, flick-screen, twin-stick-shooter, set in an alternate dimension where the pixels are still chunky, and the bad guys are black and white. Except for their dangly red bits...



BONUS!:

Also includes a full arcade game: Eugatron! 60 levels of Robotron-style, twin-stick, arena-based shooting, direct from the ‘80s and remixed for your pleasure. Do you have what it takes to become a Eugenius?



FEATURES:

-  50+ challenging rooms
-  A plethora of power-ups
-  Bonus arcade-game: Eugatron
-  Brand new Amiga exclusive soundtrack
-  Exclusive Amiga game ending
-  Highly configurable controls
-  30 achievements to collect
-  Leaderboards, statistics and achievements
-  Easter eggs galore

448487.overview: Castle Quest is an old school text adventure game.

448600.overview: A freeware game from Giovanni Iacobelli and released in 2021. The goal is to run away and not get caught while searching for the key that will open the door to the next room of the basement of the castle. There are 10 levels. Written in C++ and joystick enabled.

448881.overview: Can the Amiga run Crysis? Let's find out. The idea for this game came to me towards the end of development of Trans-Pennine Express Simulator. I figured all I needed to do was record some game footage, and pause and display a picture whenever there was something for the player to do or shoot.

448987.overview: Practice for high-school level readers; helps prepare for college aptitude tests and increase your knowledge.

448992.overview:
How to play “CARAVAN”, after the game starts, the playing area is displayed. Use your joystick to move the basket and collect the balls that fall from above. By pressing the joystick lever downwards, you can load the camels. The camel must always be directly under your basket. Different numbers of camels must be loaded with several balls per level. The number of balls varies depending on the level.

If you catch a ball in your basket, several objects can be shot:
Ducks to gain life energy
Aggressive Bedouin Fighters (only possible with the blue ball)
Witch (only with the brown ball)
By the way, the game consists of an infinite number of levels.

448997.overview: A German-language game created using the 3D Construction Kit by Virtual Fiction (J. Hunke).  In it you navigate the titular castle, fighting the dark horrors that infest the walls. It was initially released as Shareware then converted to public domain\freeware by the author in 1993, before a wide release.

448999.overview: Basically a 15-puzzle slider on steroids, this variation was written by W. Neumann and sold commercially as both Licenceware, direct and as a coverdisk on Amiga Fun magazine, released on Amiga Fun issue 5. Contact - a fascinating game that is truly addictive! For masterminds and quick thinkers. Countless game levels and numerous line ups never let you get bored!

449000.overview:
A horse racing management\statistics game published by Selec in 1987. COURSEWINNER allows you to use the power of your computer to get the edge on the bookmaker.

The program contains a database full of detailed information on all English and Scottish courses (Flat or National Hunt). The ten leading trainers and jockeys, and effect of the draw for different going, weight carried and race length is detailed for each course. This information can be displayed on the screen for reference at any time.

COURSEWINNER can be used in two modes - quick mode requires only the starting price and results of recent outings (as found in any newspaper) for each runner. Extended mode allows detailed analysis of the following factors: recent form and starting price, weight carried and race length, trainer and jockey form for the course and effect of the draw and of the going.

COURSEWINNER automatically utilises these variables and calculates a profit factor for each runner. The best bet is given, together with any other runners which appear to offer a profit at the price. 

Analysis normally requiring hours of cross referencing can be done in seconds. COURSEWINNER can help you maintain a steady profit throughout the season. 

The package comes complete with program, database and detailed instruction booklet.

449006.overview: A series of mini-games to help you learn about Christopher Columbus, along with testing to confirm your new knowledge.

449009.overview: Comprehensitr Grammar Review I — contains over 200 exercises on identifying the parts of speech, the subject and the predicate, sentence fragments, kinds of sentences, making the verb and the subject agree, etc. Grade seven and above. The game was primarily sold via magazine adds\mail order.

449010.overview: Count-It or Reken Maar is an educational math game for one player, developed and published by Action Media, which was released in 1990. It helps walk you through doing basic math sums.

449436.overview: In Cardiac Arrest! you are presented with a patient who may or may not having heart issue or a heart attack and you must troubleshoot the issue and present the right diagnosis. You can choose the difficulty of the patient, if they are pediatric or presenting a specific problem so that you might get a feel for how the scene may lay itself out. You get their emergency chart and EKG, pulse rate, blood pressure, and if they are responsive and must choose the course of action in this text game from Bruce Argyle aka The Mad Scientist in 1988.

449639.overview: A German Language text adventure with RPG elements, which was loosely based on 'Das Schwarze Auge' (The Dark Eye), this was Released on Amiga Supergame issue #4 (Logo Software publisher) in 1990 and created by R. Werner.  The player character in this text based adventure has various characteristics such as courage, strength, skill, etc.

449646.overview:
Colossal Adventure takes its cue from the very earliest mainframe text adventures. Our hero must rescue the elves and find fifteen pieces of treasure. There are many dark areas, so lights and batteries are at a premium. Be careful of vicious dwarves, who can be killed using axes. You can carry up to four objects at a time; the useful ones include a newspaper, keys and sandwiches. The vocabulary includes saying spell names, DROPping items to stay within the carrying limit (and for other specific reasons), CATCHing a bird, and standard directions plus IN and OUT.
 
COLOSSAL ADVENTURE, only available as part of the JEWELS OF DARKNESS compilation on the Amiga, enhances the original text-only incarnations released for 8-bit platforms by adding graphics, more extensive text descriptions, an extended parser that understands many more commands and other user-friendly features (e.g. multitasking, a quit back to WB option).

COLOSSAL ADVENTURE is the first installment in Level 9'sMiddle-Earth Trilogy, which also contained ADVENTURE QUEST and DUNGEON ADVENTURE. The Middle-Earth Trilogy was later published in enhanced form as a compilation and renamed to JEWELS OF DARKNESS, albeit with references to Tolkien changed or removed, reportedly, for legal reasons.

COLOSSAL ADVENTURE was Level 9's adaptation of the first computer text-based adventure game ADVENTURE (aka ADVENT, COLOSSAL CAVE, COLOSSAL CAVE ADVENTURE), written by Will Crowther in 1975/76 and enhanced by Don Woods in 1977. Originally released for the DEC PDP-10 mainframe computer and containing almost 300k of Fortran code, the game was strongly influenced by J.R.R. Tolkien. COLOSSAL ADVENTURE draws even more inspiration from Tolkien's writings and features an enlarged master game with an additional 70 locations, and a more detailed outside world than the original.

449681.overview:
A shareware game created by Jens Neubauer under the company name BauerSoft. The distributed version supports one player, 2 players are unlocked with a shareware donation. Following the great example of Hollywood Pictures comes
here the small effort called CINEMA. A successful planting of the Persia flag on the world of Hollywood in a nerve challenging Economic strategy simulation from the world of the cinema. The full version will be released as SK-GOLD !

449748.overview: A 1988 version of Connect Four, created in C by Fred Mitchell of MitchellWare Systems. This version of Connect four is for one or two players. Players take turns dropping a checker into any empty slot in the top row of the grid. The checkers fall straight down and occupy the lowest available space in the column. The first player to get four checkers in a row, either horizontally, vertically, or diagonally, wins

449753.overview: CrossMaze is a puzzle game by James Kevin Butts for one or two players. Determine by the number of letters and arrangement, how the 2 lists of words representing words going down and across intersect. It will be possible to put all the target words into the puzzle. You can save and load previous games, print them out in case you work better with pencil and paper, you can choose a list of 10, 20 or 30 words that need to be arranged and determine if there is a timer per word in place in the game.

449754.overview: The idea is to rearrange the pieces on the right hand part of the board onto the left hand side so that all the adjacent edges match.

449758.overview: A 1997 AMOS based game of American Checkers (Droughts), created by Thomas Powell. A game for one or two players, with custom colored pieces available, also allowed game tracking statistics.

449761.overview:
Cocker is a kind of breakout game for 1 or 2 players. Simple but funny. You can chose one out of 5 control methods. It was created and uploaded as freeware to Aminet in 1999 by Niels Böhm aka Mr. WC. The aim is to keep a ball inside the playing field, using a bat, and possibly bump away the blocks on the appropriate side in order to remove the whole bunch
of them, what enables you to advance to the next level and - eventually - to win the game. But it's VERY hard not to let the ball slip away behind you. Further on you have to try not to hit the blocks on the opponent's side, because for doing so the latter one will be rewarded with twice the points you would get for hitting the correct blocks on your side. BTW, the darker
the blocks are the more points are scored by hitting them. Of course, you can collect several Xtras. How? Well, they are released by smashing away the black blocks, whereupon they start to float into that players direction who most recently reflected the ball. But be warned, not every black block reveals a positive Xtra :-) And, last but not least, there is a cheat mode you can activate SOMEHOW...

449771.overview: A puzzle shooter mix. You have 20 balls to reach the required score on each level or it's game over.  Easier said then done. Hit the score requirement and head off to the next level.

449772.overview:
An adaptation of the traditional card game, for one player against a computer rival, where each side attempts to beat the opponent to the goal of 121 points.

To start with, the deck is cut and the lowest card determines who deals first. Each side receives six cards, discards two to the crib, then both take turns playing their hand to the board - attempting to score by bringing the total value to 15 or 31, and by completing certain card combinations that score additional points. "Go" is called if no cards can be played without going over a total of 31, and the attempt is transferred to the opponent; the last player to place a card gets an additional point.

When all cards have been played, both hands are scored according to their contents and special combinations, and the score for the crib goes to its owner (each side gets the crib on alternating turns). A new round begins, and so on until one of the players hits a total of 121 or above - winning the game. Board Arrows and Muggins can be toggled off or on.

449785.overview: A 1993, single player puzzle game created by Søren Holbech and released as freeware on December 19, 2023. Søren Holbech made Chillion based on the C64 version of Crillion. You control a bouncing ball, by bouncing over the blocks the same color as your ball, you can clear them and go to the next level. You can only bash blocks the same color as the ball, the white outlined blocks will change your color, these do not need to be removed. Wall blocks act as a barrier, skull blocks will cause you to lose a life. You start the game with four lives and can earn more as you play.

449823.overview:
A shareware action game created by Paul Fortin, as C&P Software in 1988. Cat & Mouse is a game for kids 6 to 99 years old.  It will entertain you for hours on end (We Hope).  I got hooked on the game after I was introduced to it on the TI-99, and I hope that you will like it just as much as I did.  
 
Cat & Mouse is a game of hand/eye coordination.  The aim of the game is very simple: STAY ALIVE AS LONG AS POSSIBLE. BUT (because there always has to be a BUT) as in real life, the more you eat the 	slower you will go and that's what your deadly opponents the Cats are hoping for. Also, if you don't eat enough you will loose your reserves of energy and either die or get caught.  Also like in real life, you only have one life to live...  The mouse is controlled by joystick.  The gauge of how well you have done is in the time that you manage to stay alive(i.e.: 60 seconds is a good game, and 90 seconds is entering the expert category. As time progresses, the speed increases and the cats since they get there proper exercise become better mousers.  Also since all that running is good for you, you will lose weight 5lbs every 5 seconds. 

	Happy Mousing!!!

450054.overview: Although this product will run under either the 1.1 or 1.2* operating system, for best results the author strongly гесоммеnds that you use Kickstart 1.1 if possible. Beat the dealer in do-or-die blackjack or solo a round of solitaire. A shareware game written by David Upson and sold in 1987.

450067.overview:
Licensed edutainment software title based on the Mad Libs children's books, written by Roger Price & Leonard Stern and printed by then-publisher Price Stern Sloan. Distributed in the U.S. by Electronic Arts. Computer MAD LIBS is an exciting new version of the MAD LIBS game you already love to play! New twists and surprises await you as computer technology is applied to the "World's Greatest Party Game." The eight MAD LIB stories on the computer disk utilize a revolutionary, built-in speech technology that allows you to hear your stories with hilarious results. Each story is illustrated with delightful cartoon graphics that add to the fun! You can edit and save any MAD LIB you create and hear it as many times as you like! Get ready for hours of fun! 
 

MAIN MENU CHOICES
MAD LIB Titles: Select this Main Menu option, and you will see the titles of the MAD LIB stories on this disk. Click on the MAD LIB title of your choice and get ready to play!
Mystery MAD LIBS: Select Mystery MAD LIBS and you are ready to play, but in this case you have no idea what the story is about. Get ready for some surprising results!
Library: Make this selection, and you will be able to choose a title from a list of all the MAD LIB stories you have saved on your disk.
Quit: Select Quit when you are finished playing MAD LIBS

450088.overview: Celestial Caesars aka Celest is a 1992 freeware strategy game by Tony L. Belding for up to nine players. This simple wargame pits you against any combination of human or computer opponents. The game uses an Intuition interface, and can be played by file-mail.

450245.overview: A freeware game created by David Hobbs (Hobbsie) in 1991, this is a pac-man clone, created in AMOS and distributed by APDC.

450267.overview: A freeware version of Mastermind with a Hi-Score table and  full  instructions from Graham Woodcock in 1991.  You start by having to guess two colors then three and  so on until you have to guess six.  At five numbers it starts to get more difficult. Codes given show if right color, wrong color, right or wrong position.

450295.overview:
A freeware AMOS game created by George R. Merritt and released in 1992. Coordination is a 30 level game played with the mouse only. The idea of Coordination is to block the path of the ball with the bat and reach the exit without touching any of the barriers. A life is lost if the ball touches any barrier. 

You must block the path of the ball, if you attempt to hit the ball, it will be pushed beneath the bat and go off in the wrong direction. It is possible to push the ball along but control will soon be lost if attempt to do so. The exits are usually on the screens boundary, indicated by a break in the barrier. On some levels the exit may be in the center of the screen and is easily recognized.

450296.overview: This  is a 'Pairs' puzzle game where you have to match a card from the top half of the screen with one from the bottom of the screen.  There is a choice of  pictures  to  use, these include cars, patterns, smileys, and flags. You  may  play  against  the  computer  in which case you can choose the number  of  tries  allowed per game, or there is a 2 player option.  You can  also  choose  between  18  or  32 pair to be matched.  All in all a nicely done game, created by Graham Lund (Lundy) with AMOS in 1992 and released as freeware. Can be found in APD383. Instructions for using your own pictures are included.

450297.overview: Creepy Crawley is a novel game from Frank Dudley.  You control a spider who has to  eat the flies it catches in its web.  Watch out in later levels, the flies  fight  back!   Both of these programs are useful for beginners to look  at, as usual, the code is on the disk for you to look at.  This is the sort of program which can be played around with to see how it works. Packaged in APD473 with Amos Invader.

450298.overview: Not to be confused with the *other* 1990 shooter called Cross Fire, this one was for just one person, was created by Roger North and features a setup very much like the Llamasoft game Gridrunner. Your objective is to shoot the baddies on screen, while picking up goodies all the while avoiding the shots from the guns outside the grid that put pressure on you from all sides.

450354.overview: An AMOS based Shareware space strategy game from Tony Kingsmill under the name Single Cell Software in 1995. Was distributed with a hangman style game called Bottles. The full version contained various skill levels\scenarios and a save game facility. Futuristic, strategic combat!

450356.overview: An AMOS based puzzle\picture reconstruction game created by Mike Wellman and published by Courbois Software in 1991. Move the picture segments around to recreate the original image and be rewarded with another new image to recreate.

450394.overview: The rules to this word puzzle game are simple. Three letter words are worth 5 points. Four letter words are worth 10 points. Use joy stick to move the letter around and position top left of letter in center of share you want to paste into. Words go across, down and through the 3D tiers. It is possible to score more than one word on a turn.

450445.overview: Hit Or Miss, Magic, More Clocks, Pairs, Pairs, Scorpion, Set The Clock, Tower Of Hanoi, Yukon

450452.overview:
A collection of solitaire card games developed by David A. Lorner and released into the public domain 1992.

The games included are:

Beleaguered Castle, Clock, Eight Off, Flower Garden, Fourteen Out, King Albert, Patience, Scoreline, Sir Tommy,Snap, Strategy, Tray, Windmill

450527.overview: A freeware card based memory game created by Tropic Design (Hanns Holger Rutz) in 1993. Search the cards and match sets of two. Clear the board and you can do it again!

450562.overview: A freeware puzzler from Pawel Karwasz in 1992. Use the control switches to get all your lemming-like buddies to one of the teleporters safely, the more mites make it the higher your score. In some cases, teleporters can only be used once, or dangers may appear mid-level like deadly stalagmites. Once you have saved all your kin, head out the teleporter yourself.

450768.overview: 4'n Row 3D is a 1991 freeware release from Multibug software for two players. Try to get 4 colors in a row, horizontally, vertically, diagonally across 4 playing surfaces. It was released on several PD compilations including by The Assassins and the 1993 "Now That's What I Call Games" compilation.

451570.overview: A Sequel to CRYSTAL HAMMER. It contains 50 levels compared to 30 levels in the original game.  Like the original version, this updated and improved version, is all about reflecting a ball against a wall of bricks. Behind the wall of bricks live some worm-like creatures that will come out to disturb you when you've opened a hole in the wall. Prolonged contact with the creatures will kill your bat. Destroying bricks will often cause a coloured brick to come spinning down slowly. These spinning bricks are power-ups, altering your ball or bat according to their colour. You can have a sticky bat (green), a wide bat (blue), a slower ball (yellow), multiple balls (cyan), and the decidedly Arkanoid-inspired shooting bat (red). Whatever you do, don't pick up the grey brick, or you will be destroyed.

451647.overview:
A freeware, AMOS based, text adventure created by Scott Lebrun in 1992. Australian Scott Le Brun wrote various text adventure games, initially for the VZ200 and VZ300 in BASIC. A VZ version of this game dates to at least as early as 1988. 
The 1992 Amiga conversion was produced using AMOS and is a fantasy based game where you must find your way into a daunting castle, filled with the cursed undead. It even includes an atmospheric music track to listen to while you play.

451649.overview: A shareware game by Harald Wagner and released in 1993. Find the keys, avoid the monsters and make your way to the next level. Released as part of Spielekiste 289 and apparently this key combination is important to having a blast.... N B A R K W J T U E. Have fun!

451650.overview: A variation upon Shanghai that takes a lot of liberties with the "traditional" concept, replacing the classic mahjongg tiles with new ones with a more modern, more colourful theme including pictures of records, film reels, sparkplugs and even the Commodore logo. There are fifteen different layouts to choose between, and a level editor should you tire. There is a undo function, and a cheat function to remove tiles from the screen. China Tiles is a freeware AMOS game created by Stephen Hughes in 1993.

451651.overview: A freeware game for two called Circles Up written in C and released as Open Source. Described as a successful game of skill for 2 players, based on the classic game "Four wins" aka 4 Gweinnt or Connect Four.

451652.overview: Clear-Game : About tricky thinking and sliding game of the most challenging type. You must remove all tiles from the board by linking a series of identical images. But be careful! There is the limited time.  A shareware game, written in C with a game editor included, also published by Sigmar Computer. Created by Peter Händel and released in S p i e l e k i s t e # 475.

451653.overview: A freeware chess game (Schach) that had several versions, including v2.02 which was dated 1989 and was created by John Stanback, Bob Leivian, and Alfred Kaufmann and written entirely in C.

451654.overview:
A text based strategy game created by Russell Wallace and released as shareware in 1988, inspired by a game called Ganymede back on the 3. 5K Vic-20 but obviously a huge improvement on that game.  

In the game, you are in charge of a mining base on Jupiter's Moon, Callisto. The moon itself contains nothing more valuable than nice and dirt, but valuable minerals can be obtained from the atmosphere of Jupiter itself by robot mining stations (human workers could not survive the conditions there). Your job is to collect the ore produced and bring it to the moon using short-range nuclear drive spacecraft. From there it can be collected by long-range ion drive ships for your employers, the Interplanetary Mining Corporation. You will be paid for the ore and must use this money to buy various equipment and plutonium fuel to run it.  
 
WARNING - if you run out of fuel, your food/oxygen recycling machinery will not be able to function and everyone on the base will die. 

Sounds simple enough, but there are other difficulties several competing companies have also set up mining bases in the vicinity of Jupiter. Far beyond the jurisdiction of the Earth police, anything goes and while the robot mines themselves are concealed in t the depths of Jupiter's atmosphere your base is vulnerable to attack. Computer-controlled laser batteries can be purchased for defense. Also, spacecraft can be equipped with combat computers, shielding and nuclear cannon so that they can be used for attacking enemy bases as we as setting up mines and retrieving ore. You will be paid for damage done. Each ship can carry 2 nuclear warheads on a mission.

451658.overview: Crypto-King is a Shareware puzzle game created by Robert Bromley in 1991.  A game for those who like to solve Cryptograms, (those coded sentences that have to be decoded to be read). This version of Crypto-King which will search 100 Cryptogram databases and will contain at least two 100 Cryptogram databases. The 'Scrambler' program which will enable you to create your own databases.

451659.overview: A single player, Shareware, Pac-Man clone, collect'em up created by Martin Esters with multiple levels of difficulty and a high score screen.

451660.overview: A freeware puzzle game created by Holger Brunst and distributed with AmiNet in 1993. This is like a Rubik's Cube of clocks. The hands of several clocks must be brought into the same position.

451661.overview: A freeware action game written with ASM 68k by Spider Arnaud Guyon aka Spider in 1991. A freerunner style game where you must run\jump on the colored sections and avoid the black sections. Your score increases as you continue to be able to progress forward. the longer you go, the faster the track moves under you. SPEED KILLS, so run and jump smartly.

451662.overview: A workbench playable, German-language, codebreaker\Mastermind game using numbers. The display will indicate how many right numbers you have and how many are in the right place. You have an impending time limit, so think fast! This freeware, puzzle game created by Horst Wiegmann in 1993.

451663.overview: A freeware solitaire game created by Michael Hartmann and released by Spielekiste (Berlin PD) in 1992.

451665.overview: A 1992 early math and numbers freeware game from Ken Winfield. Counting Fun is for one player and is a simple sums game. Released as part of #2723 Assassins Back to School 1 and in the Fish Disks.

451666.overview: A freeware puzzle game created by Norbert Ossenkopp in 1991. In this one person game the aim is to place 32 colored double-stones on the game board so that no stone remains. The Amiga has randomly distributed the stones on the board but what is their position. Place a stone on the game board, click on the game piece with the mouse arrow. A frame appears that shows the stone position, rotation is done with the right mouse button. Left click places the stone, click on a placed stone to delete it. there are three levels of difficulty in this thinking game and a timer to push your thinking faster.

451670.overview: A Car Business simulator with three levels of difficulty. Build a thriving car business around the world, invest, purchase raw materials and keep parts that will allow for fluctuations in availability. Rule the world.

451672.overview:
Chaos: Battle of the Wizards  is a fantasy strategy game written by Sean Irvine and released as freeware in 1995. In it you are a wizard who battles it out against up to seven other wizards that can be both player and/or computer controlled. The last one alive wins. The game is turn based and each turn is divided in two parts. In the first you select and cast spells and movement is done in the second.

There are several different spells available. Some of them let you summon creatures to attack the opponent while others will improve your abilities or are offensive (like lightning) or defensive (summon castles). Summoning spells would include Centaurs and Horses, which can be mounted by the wizard and enable you to move across the playing board quickly. Spells can also be either Lawful, Neutral or Chaotic, so the chances of success increase if the wizard has the same alignment.

451677.overview: A French-language, freeware, single person target shooter created with CanDo by Alain Ceccato in 1994

451678.overview: An AMOS based, freeware puzzle game from Stan Thomas. Choose the size of the board, and therefore the difficulty and change the clocks to all match in a certain number of moves.

451679.overview:
CBridge 4.0D aka Contract Bridge 4.0 from Sydenham Software (Errol Wallinggford) was a shareware release in 1992, where the free demo was 15 minutes of play before it timed out. It was released in S p i e l e k i s t e   # 214  and in ASI-GAMES-VOL 257. Contract Bridge is a single player, shareware, implementation of the card game of the same name.

The player can choose to play as the South hand, West North or East. The game, which uses US style practices uses the Goren Point-Count method for hand evaluation and recognizes these conventions; Short Club Openers, No Trump Weak Signal Bids, Preemptive Opening bids, Stayman, Take-Out Doubles, and Blackwood though any or all of these conventions can be turned off.

The game opens with a suit bid on hands that have thirteen or fourteen points and a four card suit, or sixteen to eighteen points for a one no trump bid. After each hand the player can replay it, review it, or rotate the hands and replay it.

451681.overview: The improved sequel to the original Amiga port of the vastly popular board game of checkers or droughts. In it, you can choose a one or two player game and the level of difficulty if playing against the machine. You can also show threats, forfeit moves, take moves back and swap sides for a better view from your opponent's perspective. Like the original it is Shareware, make by Pete Storonskij and this one was released in 1995.

451682.overview: Written by the experienced Chess game creator, Bill Jordan, this game was written in BASIC and while light on the graphical stylings it was heavy on quality moves by the computer. Bill has written several chess related programs, amongst others Chess Teacher 1.2, Chess Rater and Chess Analyzer and still updates his chess page that touts that it has, "More on chess than any website in the world. "

451683.overview:
A freeware AmigaBASIC game created by Russell Mason in 1991, this triangle puzzle, also called the golf tee game (or more modernly the Cracker Barrel Tee game, Hi-Q or Peg Solitaire), has a history that goes back to the court of Louis XIV and beyond and challenges you to jump one peg over the other and removed the jumped peg, remove all but one of the pegs and you win. Place a peg in each of the holes of the game board. You’ll have one place on the board that won’t have a peg.

Jump one peg over another to an open space and remove the one that was jumped. Keep doing this until only a single peg remains.

If you are successful and leave only one peg, you are a “genius.”

Leave two pegs, and you’re “pretty smart.”

Leave three pegs, and you are just plain “dumb.”

But leave four pegs, and sorry, but you are an “EQ-NO-RA-MOOOSE.” (it’s all in good fun – no judgement here!) 
 
In this version you can choose which peg is left empty, which can decrease or increase the complexity in ways that are surprising.

451684.overview:
A single player game emulating a casino experience created by Robert D'Asto and published in 1992 as freeware. The goal of each player is to win the pot, which contains all the bets that the players have made in any one deal. A player makes a bet in hopes that they have the best hand, or to give the impression that they do. In most Poker versions, the top combination of five cards is the best hand. 
 
Five cards are dealt to each player plus another hand of five cards face down on the table. Cards are turned up one at a time, and there is a round of betting each time a card is exposed. Each player selects a hand of five cards from among the cards in their own hand and the five on the table. The game uses standard poker hands.

451685.overview: A freeware 15-slider-puzzle game from David Cole in 1988 where you unscramble the colored cobra images.

451686.overview: A freeware platform game created by Christian Krauss (Castley) in 1990 for one player. Version 1.1 would be released in 1993. Distributed in Saar Disk #617: Courli + Spider and by The Assasins disk 194. This is a Crillion like ball game where you must safely bounce to remove the colored blocks without touching the skull\poison blocks.

451689.overview: A shareware game from Jeff Sprague, created in 1993. This shooter is a bit like an AMOS version of Tempest. Electrical surges are pulsing through the power grid of the central defense computer network. You must detect and neutralize them before the reach the outer line. Unstopped surges will drain your energy until the network fails.

451690.overview: A snake\lightcycle game from  John G. Gilmore in February of 1987, written entirely in C and released as freeware. The game had three levels of difficulty. Use the arrow cursor keys or the keypad combo of 8, 5 to go up and down 4 and 6 to go left and right. In the game you avoid other cycles and lines and try to trap the other cycles with your lines and those of other players. In case of emergency, you can run into the box outlined in pink. this will give you another chance at completing the same level. The amount of time you take to trap the other cycle and the difficulty of the level will determine the points awarded.

451711.overview: A shareware puzzle game from Pete W. Storonskij, released in 1994. Conundrum (which would be followed by Conundrum 2.0) is an abstract hexagonal based board game, where the object is to negate all of the colored tiles by placing them next to each other. This game was inspired by those hexagonal floor tiles you find on restroom floors. Once you start you have 10 seconds to place a tile, each tile ranges from 1 to 10, having its own color configuration. The number on the tile is the number of negations that must be done on it. Tiles are negated by placing them side by side. The game starts with six negations per tile and can be negated from any adjacent position. The number of tile types starts slowly to allow you to understand the game play. You are given tiles and exploding tiles to play with.

451712.overview: A 1995 transmutation of the strategy\tactics game created by Epyx for 8 bit machines. This shareware version by Ronald Picardi in 1995 was created in AMOS and likewise lets you assume the role of a movie-style monster, becoming a kaijin titanic horror. Technically CC&C is a strategy game; you have to keep an eye on several statistics, including your health, appetite, and even such minute details as the tilt of your head (helps in aiming breath weapons). Destroy the city before the human military destroys you!

451729.overview:
Originally released by Marco Pinto in 1992 as shareware, this AMOS title went to freeware as of version 5 in 1999. Have you ever wanted to create adventure games? Well now you can on your Amiga. This package gives you the ability to create adventure games similar to those that we all loved to play on our 8-bit computers with ease.

Features:
* Include up to 11 pieces of music
* Up to 65536 screens with graphics
* Create up to 65536 Rooms / Messages
* Create up to 256 System Messages
* Create up to 256 Objects
* Save your finished Adventure as an Executable
so that it will run without CAG

451763.overview: Crossword Puzzle Creator, created by Jurgen Weinelt and presented in German language, it had several versions, with the last version, v5.1 (Cross) released in 1993, the original version came out years prior. Version 3.3 was released on PD U1421. It allowed the creation of basic crossword puzzles without fancy graphics.

451860.overview: A memory game created by James of AARUG in 1990. Find the matches to win!

451988.overview: Crossword Puzzle (CWP) was written by Mike Epting and distributed on Aminet as Freeware in 1992. This crossword game was written entirely in C. The game can be played from the workbench. For tough solutions you can get a single letter hint or check your solution at any time. If you wish to save a puzzle in mid game that is available. You can enter your own puzzles using a text editor. The first line is the height and width of the puzzle in squares e.g. 13, 13. The next lines are the puzzle solutions. Use upper or lower characters but be careful abut the spaces. To make this thing square you will probably need spaces at the end of some lines. The game was distributed via AmiNet and Genie.

451997.overview: An unfinished Command & Conquer Clone By Daniel Allsopp, released to Aminet as Freeware in 1997.  A real-time strategy (RTS) game. The control system involves selecting units with the mouse and then directing them, while the opponents make their moves without waiting for a "turn" to end. You must build buildings, that have game functions to allow you to progress and create fighting units to control.

452100.overview:
A freeware AMOS game created by Robert W. Benjamin in 1997. Welcome to Cavern Commander. This game is a shoot'em-up scroller, completed in 4 weeks. The inhabitants of a 5 level underground cavern are in trouble. The defense system has gone hay-wire. When ships try to deliver food to the inhabitants of the cavern the defense systems destroy them. The Creatures, men and animals are slowly starving.  
 
You must rescue the creatures with your ship while avoiding the cavern walls, missiles and killer satellites, all the while picking up and saving anyone or anything you can. To make things worse, you must constantly watch your fuel meter. Your ship will fire in the direction you are facing and you have one ship in reserve. To refuel, simply touch the fuel tank with your ship. Advance to higher levels by rescuing all the creatures.

452101.overview: Car battle is a fun blasting game for two to five players at once (with adapter). Created as freeware by Jools Henn in 1997. Shoot or smash your opponents and take them out. Grab power ups and avoid. When all but one car is left, you'll get a tally of the hits. Set up tallies and leaderboards for big party fun!

452305.overview: In Collision Course Alpha, the aim is to last as long as possible. This is a work in progress version of a e-mailware game that I have been messing around with. Just click on the icon and use the cursor keys to turn your yellow arrow thingy. Up accelerates and (q) is self destruct. This Version (April 98) has a GUI frontend, and a high-score table. The high score table is placed in your script directory (sys:s/). The game  now forces a PAL screenmode.

452307.overview: Released as freeware as a, "work in progress" as Cyber Cardz 0.2 by Marco Guidone in 1998 this solitaire game was intended to display the excellent card artwork as much as provide the user with a fun and immersive pass time game.

452559.overview: An unfinished AMOS freeware Tetris puzzle game from Krzysztof Pichlak for one player.  The screen info is in Polish, but easy to play for any language speaker. Don't let the unfinished part scare you away, this is a quality Tetris game.

452738.overview:
A game of ability that will put a strain on our dexterity in managing the mouse. In fact, we will have to unite all the squares, in increasing order, without running into the penalties caused by unwary movements or touching the wrong numbers. An AmigaBASIC game published in Commodore Computer Club #66 in July of 1989 on Page 44. The game works with Microsoft AmigaBASIC. 

Starting from box 1, by clicking with the mouse inside the same, you have to join all the other boxes in ascending order and finally touch the celestial ball in the center. Beware of abrupt movements and stay too long with the mouse inside the boxes themselves: the penalties will increase inexorably.
Also pay attention to the order with which you touch the boxes, touch the wrong ones in fact, makes the value of the penalty exponentially increase.
Ah, I forgot, try to spend as little as possible on the lines already drawn, even this, guess what, adding a little, will add penalties...
In short, hand still and strong nerves!
Choose the difficulty from 0 to 6 and... Have fun!

454669.overview: Orginally a dedicated handheld re game developed by company TOMY Ltd. from Japan and relased in 1982.

454991.overview: One screen Asteroids-like shooter.  Play to be on top of the hi-score table. Created using RedPill for Christmas in 2024.

458463.overview: cyberTRON is a tron light cycles type game for 2 to 4 players on Commodore Amiga.

458828.overview: A text-adventure game for AGA Amiga computers

460597.overview: Drug Wars is another in the long line of traditional American Laser Games arcade-conversion shooters.

460601.overview: Crime Patrol is a live-action laserdisc video game released by American Laser Games in 1993.

461839.overview:
The third and final game this time is Knight. The game play is unmistakably reminiscent of chess. After listening to Sir Archibald's presentation, you have two options: either press the space bar to listen and see the instructions, or press <RETURN> to start the game. If you choose to follow the instructions, the various movement options for the Knight in chess appear on the screen. Once you understand the mechanics, or if you already know the rules of chess, you can press the left mouse button. Then, position yourself on a square on the board and press the mouse button again. Now the game begins. A counter will track the moves you manage to make; the skill lies in avoiding a situation where you are caught with no moves left and, of course, in occupying as many squares as possible.

Published in the AmigaMagazine OnDisk #03 in November 1988.

461927.overview:
Colors is a fun game, very similar to the very famous Russian game Tetris.
The rules are simple, also because we have only one rule, to construct sequences of at least three blocks horizontally, vertically, or diagonally of naturally the same color. When sequences are formed, blocks are deleted from the screen and the score is incremented. You can choose a game level from 1 to 9, at each level everything speeds up.

AmigaMagazine OnDisk #19-20 in January 1991.

462222.overview: I had the preview (for gameboy) now here is a barely working demo but hey, its my cuckoo clock idea (starting to test out mechanical movement, where character moves ahead or back when hitting certain blocks)!

462304.overview: The game is inspired by the great 8-bit classics Manic Miner and Jet Set Willy by Matthew Smith.

462317.overview:
Corkers Compilation for the Amiga contains the following four games:

- Blob
- Wonder Dog
- Blastar
- Cyberpunks

462403.overview: CALLBACK is a fast-paced Arkanoid-style action game.

464455.overview: The player controls a blue mouse and the aim is to collect all the cheese to move onto the next level whilst avoiding the 4 patrolling cats.

465845.overview: The story is still the same, and nothing new has been added to the game per say. The graphics has been upped for the Amiga release, and we have tried to give the player the same feeling from the C64 version. More or less. Well, that's how ports works, well in my head at least. :P Anyway. Hope you like this C64-Amiga port.

469079.overview: A 1 to 4 player, party game best played with humans. An elimination game where the lowest ranked player each day is eliminated.

469485.overview: CYBER BLAST – Classic Amiga Action Reignited!

469961.overview: The game is inspired by the legendary arcade game Space Invaders and the not so known Space Monster made for the Videopac G7000 by Philips.

471161.overview: The Grayscale Armada has drained the color from five worlds. You pilot the Chromacraft — the last ship that can restore what was lost. This demo features World 1: Verdant Valley.

472737.overview: The game includes an original chess engine based on the negamax alpha-beta algorithm with numerous enhancements, procedurally generated chess piece graphics (no IFF files required), a full AmigaOS-style menu system using GadTools, and PGN game save/load.

473125.overview: The City of Gold part 1 is an cRPG adventure from Per Holmström (Grottkräl), author of the award winning adventure Drakborgen The Secret of Ath Ungol for Dragonbane amongst other things. The game follows the player seeking the City of Gold! Searching for adventure in a fantasy setting. It uses a modern playstyle, in a retro game engine.

476655.overview: This game is an adaptation of the Italian adventure Morgan Tyler: Il Pianeta Maledetto by Bonaventura Di Bello. It was originally written using The Quill and Illustrator and published by Edizioni Hobby S.r.l. on the cover tape of Viking, no. 2, February 1987 for the ZX Spectrum and Commodore 64.

477601.overview: MrDig’s ChipSnake is a fast, colourful take on the classic Snake formula, created specifically for the Commodore Amiga 1200.

479814.overview:
A native Amiga port of C0MAN, a Pac-Man-style game originally written for
unexpanded MSX1. Same maze, same green-on-black look, same simple bleeps -
just running on 68000 silicon instead of a Z80.

479992.overview: After your grandfather's death, you inherit an old house and a small piece of forest — along with his unpaid debt. To keep the property, you must work hard: cut down and replant trees, process wood, complete orders and develop your small lumber business before time runs out.

480158.overview: Reverse engineered 1997 game "Carmageddon" (including "Splat Pack" DLC) compiled for AmigaOS 68k

480170.overview: Porting the original Game Gear version of Columns to Amiga

480367.overview: I'd like to share an experimental native AGA conversion of Jaleco's 1985 arcade game City Connection, developed by ChatGPT-6 / Astra.

480426.overview:
First Tower Defense Game on Classic Amigas. Including Editor for new Maps.
Its Alpha with only 1 Level and 10 Waves and Boss Enemy at the end of Wave 10.

481011.overview: Welcome to the magical and frantic world of Cat in the Sky with Diamonds, a colourful psychedelic arcade game developed (more or less...) entirely in AMOS Professional by Alberto "BCO" Sgaggero for the legendary Commodore Amiga 500.

481321.overview: Celtic Survivors is an action game for the Amiga 1200 (AGA) in the spirit of Vampire Survivors. It has 256 colours, a hand-painted isometric village and hundreds of Romans on screen.

481488.overview:
Conversion of the original Sega Master System cartridge "Casino Games"
(Sega, 1989) by SHINOBIZ, with the help of Claude.

481518.overview: Atari's classic 1980s hit Centipede for OCS/ECS/AGA Amiga computers.

481590.overview: An in-game level editor for the Amiga game Cannon Fodder, as a WHDLoad install for a hard disk. You build your own missions of up to six phases in the game's own view, with the game's terrain, soldiers, vehicles and buildings, test them at once, and play them from the recruitment hill like the missions of the campaign.

481638.overview: A port of Atari 2600 classic for Amiga 500.

481654.overview:
A classic color-matching game brought to the Amiga!
The goal is to match colors, think ahead and progress through a challenging puzzle experience. Simple to understand but increasingly demanding, Coloron offers an enjoyable combination of logic, observation and planning.

481727.overview: Commander Keen 4 v1.4 EGA for AmigaOS 68k

481747.overview: Cho Ren Sha 68k is a vertical shoot 'em up for the Sharp X68000, (c) 1995 by Famibe No Yosshin. This is a port of the original game code to the Commodore Amiga: the X68000 program runs on the 68020+ with the X68000's hardware emulated in software, and its picture is shown on a graphics card (RTG) or on the AGA chipset.

481865.overview: A 16-bit remaster of the Atari 2600 classic Combat for any Amiga with 512K of chip RAM. All 27 original game variations are here with the original gameplay, now with new graphics, music, sampled sound and a computer opponent. The game uses the Amiga’s custom chips: the blitter, hardware sprites, the copper and Paula.

481968.overview: This is the Atari ST version of Chopper X running on an Amiga

482019.overview:
A medieval jewel-matching adventure for the Amiga 1200 / AGA, by Johannes Naumanen.

Journey through royal halls, frozen castles, overgrown chambers, swamps, lava and ivory. Match jewels, open new routes and choose when to unleash an arrow, a bomb, a homing special or a disco ball. Combine specials to turn a difficult position into a cascade of colour and sound.

482294.overview: The setting is World War II, and England has made and trained a small group of special elite forces called "commandos". These commandos are specially trained to take on the most crucial and risky missions. These men are sent in to covertly take out installations, sabotage plans, assassinate leaders, and cause as much disruption to the enemies of the free world.

482825.overview:
CLICK BY CLICK is a quirky, humorous clicking adventure where nothing quite goes the way you'd expect. What starts off completely harmlessly soon turns into a wonderfully absurd experience full of surprises and bizarre moments. You don't need any special skills, complicated controls or even an instruction manual. Just your mouse. And perhaps a little patience.

How hard can it possibly be to click on a tiny pixel square?
